cards.plan:
U23 plan: no-Nix machine behavior

Decision: D-JPK-NONIX1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed. Implement graceful degrade: Nix-free packages realize; packages that need the Nix bridge fail with one E12xx naming them and both fixes, install Nix or switch/adapt; realized packages are not held hostage.

Build order:
1. Split provider capability from realization failure in crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Provider.rs. Add package-focused NeedsNix facts before spawning nix. Keep ProviderError::NixMissing for unexpected direct bridge calls.
2. Change compose_env/build flows in crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/CLI.rs to collect Nix-free successes plus bridge-required holes, then emit one package diagnostic. Do not roll back realized hangar objects.
3. Cover every bridge path: Nix provider package refs, ad-hoc -p nixpkgs packages, named sources resolved to Nix, foreign flake fallback, and jet bridge flake. Keep existing E1256 for foreign-flake/bridge commands that cannot run at all without nix; add package-specific E12xx nix-bridge-required for package refs.
4. Add --json shape where relevant: realized refs plus holes, stable for CI.
5. Verify ProviderKind::Infer and Provider::uses_nix_provider never force Nix for cached/core-capable sources. Core provider and adapters must work with PATH stripped of nix.
6. Update docs/spec/diagnostics.md and docs/spec/spec.md with no-Nix package behavior and the E1256 vs E12xx distinction.

Likely touched: crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Provider.rs, CLI.rs, Output.rs if reusable coded rendering helps, Bridge.rs only to avoid drift, RefSpec.rs if classification needs bridge-needed labels, docs/spec/diagnostics.md, docs/spec/spec.md, tests/jetpack.rs, tests/env_dev_trust.rs if trust/no-Nix overlaps.

Diagnostics/tests/docs: add E12xx nix-bridge-required. What: N packages need the Nix bridge and Nix is not installed. Why: list exact refs/packages. Fix: install Nix link or replace/draft adapter with jet add <ref> --adapt. Snapshot single and multi-package forms if pluralized. Existing E1256 stays foreign-flake/bridge specific.

Targeted tests: no-Nix PATH plus core package env realizes and command runs; no-Nix PATH plus prebuilt/copy adapter runs; mixed core/adapt plus nixpkgs records Nix-free realization then emits E12xx listing only holes; jetpack enter -p postgres with no nix emits E12xx not raw spawn/E1256; foreign flake --flake and jetpack bridge flake still emit E1256; --json exposes holes and realized refs.

Gates: no raw nix spawn errors; Nix-free packages remain realized even when bridge refs fail; diagnostic registered and snapshot-pinned; targeted tests then full nix develop -c cargo test --workspace green in implementation session.

Build order:
1. Define the local discovery index schema: package source, canonical name, aliases only as typo hints, versions, resolved identity, platforms, docs, option fields, defaults, and provenance. Store as std-only JSONL or compact text under `.jet/` or hangar metadata; no compiler external crates.

4. Wire diagnostics and suggestions so unknown package refs can consult the index for nearest names, preserving current E09xx/E12xx style.
5. Add LSP hooks: completions after provider dots inside `module env.*` package lists; completions and hover for typed fields in `Service.{}` and env/module option bodies; hover uses the same index records as CLI.

cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-BUILDDBG1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Define a build attempt record: package/ref, source identity, recipe hash, platform, tool deps, step list, start/end status, scratch dir, log dir, and envelope link. Persist under `.jet/logs/build/` or hangar metadata using std-only serialization.
2. Wrap every package/adaptor build step in a runner that captures stdout/stderr per step, records command/env/cwd, timestamps, exit status, and redacts secret values. Successful scratch follows U22 cleanup; failed scratch is preserved under hangar-scoped failure storage.
3. Add `--shell-on-fail` to realize-class verbs that can build packages. On failure, open the configured shell in the preserved scratch with exact PATH/env and cwd at the failed step. In tests, allow a fake shell command so no interactive test hangs.
4. Extend `jet explain <ref>` without breaking diagnostic-code `jet explain E1234`: code-shaped args keep existing behavior; package/ref args print resolution path, provider choice, lock identity, recipe/provenance, last build status, failed step, and log path.
5. Add `jet logs <pkg>` with text and `--json`; include per-step logs, latest/attempt selection, and stable JSON schema for CI.
6. Wire the primary build-failure diagnostic to name the failed step, `jet logs <pkg>`, and `--shell-on-fail`.

Likely touched files/modules:
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Recipe,Provider,Store,Envelope,RefSpec,CLI,Shell,JSON}.rs`
- New `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/BuildLog.rs` or `BuildDebug.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/{Lock,Loader}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Adapter/build fixtures in `tests/fixtures/jetpack-typed/`; tests in `tests/{jetpack,pkg,engine_dispatch}.rs`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add E12xx build-failed diagnostic with What/Why/Fix and coverage.
- Add E12xx for missing build log/ref unknown to `jet logs` or `jet explain` if needed.
- Update `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`; add CLI help/man/completion entries through existing registry.
- Ensure log JSON schema and explain output are pinned in tests.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test attempt record read/write and redaction.
2. Fixture adapter with three steps where step 2 fails: assert scratch preserved, log files written, diagnostic names step 2 and fix commands.
3. Same fixture with fake `JETPACK_SHELL_ON_FAIL` or equivalent: assert shell command receives cwd/env/PATH and exits cleanly.
4. `jet explain weirdctl` after failure prints provider path, source hash, recipe hash, platform, failed step, scratch, log path.
5. `jet logs weirdctl --json` parses and includes per-step status/output without ANSI noise.
6. GC integration: preserved failed scratch is reachable until the configured failure retention sweep, then collectable.

Gates:
- No raw rustc/provider noise as primary UX; Jet diagnostic names the next command.
- No plaintext secrets in logs, scratch metadata, or JSON.
- Failed scratch stays in hangar-managed space, never `/tmp`.
- `jet explain ECODE` behavior remains backward compatible.

cards.title: Highlighting: one source of truth across editors
cards.body: Audit 2026-07-05: three hand-kept grammars drift — vscode tmLanguage 164 lines, tree-sitter 998, zed highlights.scm 136, vs 569 registered tokens in Syntax.rs (I7). The v5 'copy' verb (shipped S4) is highlighted in NO grammar; VS Code, Zed, and GitHub color the same file differently. Owner: 'even code highlighting doesnt seem consistent.' Decision D-HL1.
cards.plan:
Highlighting single source of truth under D-HL1=D (grammars generated from Syntax.rs + LSP semantic-token overlay, CI drift gate). Implement on master. Invariant I7: Syntax.rs is already the registry every user-typeable token must live in — this card makes that fact enforce coloring.

Build order:
1. Classify the registry: extend crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs entries with a highlight class per token (keyword.control / keyword.declaration / keyword.ownership / marker / operator / sigil / literal-prefix ...). Mechanical: a const table or attribute alongside each existing entry; no token strings move. Any token without a class = compile error in the generator, so future ratifications can't skip it.
2. Generator: `jet devtools grammars` in Source/CmdDevTools.rs. Emits BEGIN/END GENERATED sections inside: editors/vscode/syntaxes/jet.tmLanguage.json (keyword/marker/operator patterns), editors/tree-sitter/grammar.js keyword externals (or a generated keywords.js the grammar requires), editors/zed/languages/jet/highlights.scm keyword block. Hand-written structure rules (strings, comments, interpolation, blocks) stay outside the markers and are preserved byte-for-byte on regeneration. Generator is deterministic (sorted output) so regeneration is diff-stable.
3. Drift gate: tests/grammar.rs gains every_syntax_token_is_highlighted — for each user-typeable token in Syntax.rs, assert presence in each grammar's generated section, and assert the generated sections match a fresh in-memory generation (stale-file detection). Red today (copy, ^, & missing) until stage 2 output is committed. This test joins the CI PR gate (#211).
4. Semantic overlay: extend Source/LSP semantic tokens — add token types/modifiers for v5 ownership (& write-borrow, ^ move, copy verb), markers (#Test/#Unsafe/... as decorator-class), retired/foreign keywords (E03xx teaching-error spellings) explicitly NOT keyword-colored. editors/vscode/package.json semanticTokenScopes maps the new types; zed extension.toml equivalents. Fixture test: canon.jet + examples/features/memory/ownership.jet token dumps snapshot-tested in tests/lsp.rs.
5. Regenerate all three grammars, run editors/*/install.sh locally, verify canon.jet renders consistently in VS Code + Zed; screenshot pair in the card log. GitHub rendering uses the committed tmLanguage — verified by the drift test alone.
6. Docs: editors/README pointers; note in syntax-decisions.md tooling section (D-HL1=D logged); CLAUDE.md syntax-decision protocol gains one line: 'ratifying syntax = run jet devtools grammars, commit regenerated sections' (the drift test makes forgetting red anyway).

Exit criteria:
- cargo test --test grammar green, including staleness check.
- Semantic-token snapshots green for canon.jet + ownership.jet + copy_verb.jet.
- `copy`, `^`, `&`, and every S75/S76/v5 token colored in all three grammars; retired spellings (val, var, dotless construction) not keyword-colored anywhere.
- Full suite green; zed grammar-repo stays untracked (build artifact — .gitignore already covers it).

Gates: none — D-HL1 ratified 2026-07-05. No new user-typeable syntax, so no formatter work.

Delegation: stages 1–2 one sonnet agent (single subsystem); stage 4 separate agent after 2 lands; stage 3 test written FIRST (red) per workflow loop.

questions.text: Propose a potential hybrid solution that carefully combines the best of each. What do unreal and unity and godot do? What are the downsides of each approach? What do most game developers prefer? What is the best option? How can we mitigate/fix the downsides of your proposed option?
questions.answer: Hybrid proposal: choose a refined C: scene-first + component scripts + frame hook + optional systems. Shape: `Scene` is durable editable data, nodes/entities own sprites/colliders/audio/input bindings, behavior attaches as small scripts/components, and `scene.on_frame` remains the one-file beginner escape hatch. Later, high-scale code can add ECS-style systems over the same scene data; that is an expert layer, not the first tutorial. What major engines do: Unreal centers placed Actors with Components and Blueprints/C++ behavior; Unity centers GameObjects in Scenes with Components/MonoBehaviour callbacks; Godot centers a tree of Nodes saved as Scenes with scripts and per-frame callbacks. All three converge on the same product truth: visual/editor-readable scene data plus attached behavior. Downsides: callback-only is easiest but gives the visual editor no durable model; app-object is tidy code but still not naturally visual; scene-first can hide lifecycle order and get stringly/inspector-heavy; ECS-first scales but is too abstract for first-week users. Most game developers, especially Unity/Godot/Unreal users, prefer object/scene/component workflows for day-to-day creation; engine/performance specialists like ECS underneath, but not as the beginner surface. Best option: C, amended into the hybrid above. Mitigations: code-first scene declarations must round-trip into the editor; names/asset refs get typed handles not raw strings where possible; lifecycle has one clear order (`init`, `on_frame`, physics if present, draw); ECS/query APIs are available behind `core.game.systems` for advanced scale; the first tutorial still fits in one file and never says “component query” before a ball moves. Sources checked: official Unity GameObject docs, Godot Nodes and Scenes docs, Unreal Actor/Component docs.

cards.title: HTTPS by default in core.http
cards.body: core.net/core.http default build is plain-HTTP; https needs opt-in core.tls (jet-net: 'HTTPS requires a TLS feature; the default build is HTTP-only'). Nearly every real API is https — first-week beginners hit this wall. Decision D-TLS1: how TLS becomes default (vendored rustls bridge -> native post-E3, system TLS, or status quo).
cards.plan:
HTTPS by default under D-TLS1=A: rustls in the default build via the I6 FFI-bridge pattern, certificate verification pinned to system trust roots, native Jet TLS post-E3 only behind an external security-audit gate. Implement on master. Invariants: I2 (every TLS failure is a Jet-voiced diagnostic — rustls/OS error text never reaches the user raw), I4 (every new diagnostic gets a code + what/why/fix + ui snapshot), I6 (rustls rides the bridge like wasmtime/age precedents — D-DEP-CRYPTO1 governance, not a compiler dep).

Build order:
1. jet-net grows a default-on TLS path: rustls + system trust roots (rustls-native-certs-class) behind the existing fetch API in crates/jet-net; ureq's tls feature wired accordingly. Default build = https works; a no-tls build flag remains for freestanding/size-gated targets (release_gates.rs budgets re-checked — if the size budget breaks, that goes back to the owner as a question, not a silent budget bump).
2. core.http / core.net client: https URLs work in `jet run` with zero manifest. The E-code path 'https needs core.tls' dies for the client; core.tls package remains for advanced config (pinning, client certs, custom roots) per option A's decided scope.
3. Server side: extend the #17 HTTP server surface with TLS serving — API shape follows the existing ratified server surface (.tls(cert, key) style continuation of the #17 mandate; if the shape needs anything beyond a method on the existing builder, STOP and ballot it — do not invent surface).
4. Diagnostics (product copy, snapshot-pinned): new E42xx family — certificate invalid/expired/hostname mismatch, handshake failure, no trust roots found (the minimal-container case: name the fix — install ca-certificates), protocol errors. Each: docs/spec/diagnostics.md entry, jet explain page, tests/ui snapshot. The front end translates every rustls error class; an untranslated class panicking through = P0 per I2.
5. Tests without network: local test server with self-signed + valid-chain fixtures under tests/fixtures (generate once, check in; regeneration script documented); happy-path https fetch, each E42xx provoked deliberately. CI never touches the internet.
6. Example: examples/features/net/https_fetch.jet against the fixture server (env-pointed base URL so the example text reads like the real world but the test stays hermetic); golden-tested (I5).
7. Record the security gate: release-policy.md gains the D-TLS1 clause — native-TLS may replace rustls as default only after external audit + interop battery (vs rustls and OpenSSL test vectors); syntax-decisions.md logs D-TLS1=A in the stdlib section; roadmap.md deferred-registry paragraph updated (TLS line now says https default via rustls bridge).

Exit criteria:
- Fresh clone, default build: https fetch example runs (fixture server) — no package, no manifest.
- All E42xx snapshots green; jet explain covers each; diagnostics_coverage.rs enforced.
- Freestanding/size budgets green or explicitly re-balloted.
- core.tls advanced path still works (its existing tests stay green).
- Full suite green; docs (release-policy, syntax-decisions, roadmap, core-library.md) updated in the same series.

Gates: none open — D-TLS1 ratified 2026-07-05 (rustls bridge dep approved therein). Server-API shape stop-condition in stage 3 is conditional, not standing.

questions.text: What are the tradeoffs of having two separate constructors vs passing in tls as an option? Go seems to be the best in class in general -> what does community sentiment say? What do the vast majority of professionals prefer?
questions.answer: Tradeoff: separate constructors (`serve` + `serve_tls`) are extremely discoverable and match Go surface style, but they fork the API every time a new transport/config appears (`serve_h2`, `serve_unix`, `serve_mtls`, etc.). A `tls:` option keeps one server entry point and composes with future options, but can decay into a bag of knobs unless options are typed and named. Go sentiment: Go is respected because the easy path is tiny, but serious services usually graduate from convenience functions to an `http.Server`/`Transport` config object; Go docs show both: `ListenAndServe`/`ListenAndServeTLS` for convenience, custom `Server` for control, and custom `Transport` for TLS/proxy/etc. Vast-majority professional preference is not “many constructors forever”; it is “one obvious simple path, plus typed config when real deployment needs it.” Recommendation: keep D-TLSSERVE1=A, possibly sharpen it as hybrid-A: `Server.serve(addr, mux)` for plaintext and `Server.serve(addr, mux, tls: Server.tls(cert,key))` for HTTPS, with `tls` a typed option object that can later carry mTLS/client-auth/ALPN without new verbs. Mitigation: only allow a small fixed set of named options, reject unlabeled positional TLS, and document C/Go-style separate `serve_tls` as intentionally not chosen because it multiplies verbs as server config grows. Sources checked: Go net/http docs for convenience functions + custom Server/Transport.

questions.text: Give me tradeoffs of [List] and [Map, MapVal] style shorthands for the two most common types, but then the consistent rust style List<Type> for more specific collection types (HashMap<Type>, etc)
questions.answer: Tradeoff: shorthand for the two dominant containers keeps daily Jet light (`[User]`, map shorthand), while Rust-style named generics keep specific collection policy visible (`HashMap<K, V>`, `Deque<T>`). Main risk is two generic-looking systems: brackets for defaults, angle brackets for named structures. For map shorthand specifically, comma form `[K, V]` is compact but reads like a pair/tuple; colon form `[K: V]` better says key maps to value and matches map literals. I updated the ballot with both the hybrid recommendation and the exact comma-style variant as a separate option.

questions.text: What would we need to create a first class exceptional event system? Something that would be a great fit in game dev with the ability to subscribe to events, have hooks, would be great for web dev, etc.
questions.answer:
Yes. A first-class Jet event system should be its own runtime/framework feature, then Canvas projects it as Blueprint-style event graphs. The shape I would build is a typed Event<T> / Hook<T> model with four layers: (1) event declarations are ordinary Jet values or framework-owned callback slots with typed payload structs; (2) subscription returns a disposable/cancellable handle tied to owner lifetime, so game objects, UI components, and web handlers cannot leak; (3) dispatch has explicit phase/order policy: before/after/around hooks, priority only where deterministic ordering matters, once/debounce/throttle helpers as library adapters, and a clear sync vs async dispatch split; (4) failures are typed: handlers can be infallible, fallible, or cancelling, and the publisher chooses collect/log/stop-on-first-error semantics in the event type.

For game dev this gives input, collision, lifecycle, tick/frame, animation, physics, and gameplay messages. For web dev it gives DOM-like interaction events, lifecycle hooks, data-change signals, navigation, server request hooks, and reactive UI updates. For systems/server code it gives lifecycle, plugin hooks, telemetry, scheduler, and hot-reload events.

Required pieces before it is real: a std/runtime event library, typed subscription handles, lifecycle ownership rules, structured-concurrency integration, backpressure/queue policy for async events, deterministic ordering rules, diagnostics for dead subscriptions/reentrant dispatch/bad async handlers, debugger trace support, and Canvas projection/write transactions.

Best hybrid: ratify Canvas event graphs as views over ordinary callback/event functions now, then create a separate first-class Event/Hook design card for E3/E6 runtime work. Do not invent event Foo syntax inside Canvas. Let the event system be one canonical semantic model usable from source, Canvas, game dev, web dev, and server hooks.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.time ring — calendar parity with java.time/jiff
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: java.time (JSR-310) semantics and jiff (Rust) correctness. Card #53 (time depth) is done — first verify what actually shipped, then close residual gaps.

Audit list: civil Date / Time / DateTime types distinct from the ms timestamp; ZonedDateTime with a bundled, updatable IANA tzdb (DST-correct arithmetic — the thing most languages get wrong); Duration vs calendar Period distinction; RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 parse + format; custom format patterns; monotonic Instant separate from wall clock (Stopwatch exists — expose the primitive); truncate/round to unit; day-of-week/ordinal/week-based math; leap-second policy stated in docs; conversion to/from Unix ms without ambiguity traps.

Done means: the documented ring surface provably covers the JSR-310 core use-case table, with examples + golden tests per area. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).

- D-TIME-CALENDAR1=A: Hybrid: distinct time types with easy constructors. Keep separate Instant, DateTime, LocalDate, LocalTime, Duration, and Zone types so wrong-clock bugs are type errors. Add beginner constructors and parse helpers (`time.now_utc`, `time.today`, `time.seconds`) plus expert control over timezone database, monotonic clocks, fake clocks, and schedulers.

Ready state: Owner gates clear; card is ready for implementation.

cards.title: jetos: declarative VM integration-test framework (NixOS test-driver parity)
cards.body:
The NixOS VM test framework is its most-lauded infrastructure — jetos needs a better one to claim drop-in-and-better. Scope: declare a multi-host scenario in Jet (system.<host> configs + a typed test script — not strings driving Python like NixOS), orchestrate QEMU guests from the #263 harness, typed assertions (unit active, port open, file content, command output), inter-VM networking, deterministic replay + proof artifacts, failure output in Jet's diagnostic voice.

Beat-NixOS axes: typed test script with sema-checked host/service references (a typo'd service name fails at compile time), and first-class artifact/provenance capture. Builds on #262/#263 — coordinate with the jetos agent; this is a new layer, not their installer/system-core scope.
cards.plan:
Plan refreshed 2026-07-07 by codex-main.

Ratified decisions:
- D-JOS-VMTEST1=A: Hybrid: vmtest declarations as test targets. Top-level vmtest.<name> declarations are the canonical scenario surface, and the same object is also a normal test target for CI, filtering, artifacts, and package integration. Single-host smoke tests can be authored as shorthand that expands to vmtest; multi-host topology stays explicit. Beginners run one command; experts control host graph, network, replay, timeout, artifacts, and proof capture.
- D-JOS-VMASSERT1=A: Hybrid: typed host handles plus declarative check values. The test body uses typed host handles and assertion methods. Those methods also produce declarative check values/proof facts, so Studio/CI can render and replay them. Common checks stay one-line and type-checked; experts can write ordinary Jet control flow around them. String shell commands remain an explicit fallback assertion, never the default.

cards.title: jetos: module option priorities, overrides, and module disabling (mkDefault/mkForce parity)
cards.body:
Owner's config uses lib.mkForce (disable SDDM on the plasma-beta variant), lib.mkDefault (stateVersion), disabledModules (stylix kmscon), and system tags. NixOS solves multi-module option conflict with numeric priorities nobody can explain; jetos must solve it better or the module system can't compose real configs.

Scope: a ratified conflict/priority story for options set by multiple modules — default vs normal vs force tiers with typed spellings; disabling an imported module wholesale; per-variant overrides (one host, variants overriding single options); generation tags/labels; and the explain surface — "what set this value, what lost, why" wired into #323 options search. This is core module-system semantics: ballot the surface before code (D-JOS pattern). Coordinate with jetos agent's #262 module schema.

cards.title: corelib: core.regex — in-house RE2-class engine + API depth
cards.body:
D-REGEX1 already slates replacing the bootstrap regex crate with an in-house RE2-style engine before end of Epoch 3 — this card makes that trackable and adds the API gaps so the surface lands once, right.

Engine: linear-time DFA/NFA hybrid in pure Rust (later Jet), no backtracking, keeps the ReDoS-safety guarantee; comptime pattern syntax checking with Jet diagnostics (a bad pattern literal should fail at compile time, not runtime — beats every mainstream language).

cards.title: Workspace re-partition: shrink jet-driver, make placeholder crates real or fold them
cards.body:
jet-driver is ~44k lines and has absorbed three products: the compiler driver, Jetpack (Jetpack/CLI.rs ~4.5k, package engine), and JetOS (Jetpack/JetOS.rs ~7.2k). Meanwhile four workspace crates are shells: jet-queries (375 lines), jet-rt (401), jet-net (295), jet-impact (314). Epoch 4 (jetpack) and Epoch 7 (jetos) will grow these surfaces substantially — re-partition before they grow, not after.

Scope:
1. Extract Jetpack and JetOS out of jet-driver into their own crates (jet-pack / jet-os or per ratified naming canon: jetpack engine, jetos). jet-driver keeps only compile-pipeline orchestration + CLI dispatch.
2. For each shell crate decide: become real now, or fold into its owner until needed. jet-queries is the big one — it is the incremental-compilation seam; decide whether the query architecture becomes load-bearing now (retrofitting incrementality into a 268k-line compiler later is strictly worse). Produce a recommendation with the decision reasoning recorded in architecture.md.
3. Update docs/spec/architecture.md: crate map, dependency direction rules, which crate owns which pipeline stage (R1–R12 mapping).
4. Enforce direction: no back-edges (e.g. codegen must not depend on driver). Add a workspace-level check if cheap (cargo tree assertions in a test).

Strictly behavior-preserving: zero user-visible change, golden/snapshot suites byte-identical, full suite green. No owner gates expected (no user-facing syntax); if extraction forces a user-visible rename anywhere, ballot first. Sequencing note: do this card before the monster-file decomposition card touches Jetpack/JetOS/CLI files, so those files move once, not twice.
cards.plan: Order: (1) map current jet-driver module graph + who imports what (rg + cargo tree); (2) write the target crate map as a short architecture.md draft section — get it reviewed in-repo before moving code; (3) extract JetOS first (most self-contained), then Jetpack engine, then CLI dispatch cleanup — one extraction per commit, full suite green between each; (4) shell-crate verdicts: implement or fold, one commit each; (5) jet-queries decision writeup (incrementality now vs later) — this is a design recommendation, not a gate: record in architecture.md; (6) final pass: dependency-direction test, docs updated, full nix develop -c cargo test green.

cards.title: Decompose monster files: CoreLib.rs, Canvas.rs, TIR lower/emit, CheckerCoreLib.rs, JetOS.rs
cards.body:
Largest files today: crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib.rs (13.5k lines), Source/Canvas.rs (8.4k), crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/lower.rs (8.3k), crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCoreLib.rs (7.5k), crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/JetOS.rs (7.2k), Parser/Items.rs (5.7k), TIR/emit.rs (5.3k), TIR/subset.rs (5.1k), CheckerInfer/calls.rs (4.8k), Jetpack/CLI.rs (4.5k), jet-jit/src/lib.rs (4.5k). These files burn agent context every session and are where merge mistakes concentrate. Style rule already says small modules — enforce it.

Scope: semantics-preserving decomposition of every file above ~3k lines into responsibility-named submodules. Seams follow responsibility, not line count — e.g. CoreLib.rs splits by core module family (files/io/net/…), lower.rs by TIR construct family, CheckerCoreLib.rs mirroring the CoreLib split so sema and codegen stay navigable in parallel. Target ≤ ~1,500 lines per file; judgment allowed where a real unit resists splitting — record why in the commit message.

Rules: pure code motion — no renames of public items, no behavior change, no drive-by refactors. Safety net is the existing suite: golden outputs and UI snapshots must be byte-identical; full suite green after every file's decomposition (one file per commit). Sequencing: JetOS.rs, CLI.rs, and Canvas.rs only AFTER the workspace re-partition card lands, so they move across crates once, not twice; start with CoreLib.rs / lower.rs / CheckerCoreLib.rs / Items.rs, which the re-partition does not touch.

Done means: no source file above the target without a recorded justification; module maps make sense from names alone; zero snapshot diffs; full nix develop -c cargo test green. No owner gates.
cards.plan: Order: (1) CoreLib.rs — split by core.* family, mod.rs keeps the registration table; (2) CheckerCoreLib.rs — mirror the same family split; (3) TIR lower.rs then emit.rs then subset.rs — split by construct family (items, exprs, patterns, control flow, closures, tasks); (4) Parser/Items.rs + CheckerInfer/calls.rs; (5) jet-jit/src/lib.rs; (6) wait for re-partition card, then JetOS.rs, Jetpack/CLI.rs, Canvas.rs inside their new homes. Per file: read wholly first, write the module map, mechanical motion, cargo test --test golden + targeted suites, one commit; full suite at card close.

cards.title: Canvas frontend redesign — implement ratified family
cards.body: Implement the ratified Canvas frontend redesign as the next E6 Canvas slice. Build the modified hybrid surface: Workbench-style project/file viewer, hybrid code/split/graph editor, context-command model, UE5-style node/pin visual language, hover-only types, compact getter capsules, embedded simple variables, graphite styling, and detail toggles. Source remains the only semantic truth.
cards.plan:
# Plan: Canvas modified hybrid UI

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-CANVAS1 outcome E with owner modifications.
- Existing E6 Canvas architecture and protocol from #352; do not introduce a graph asset or GUI-owned semantics.

Scope:
- Source/Canvas/html.rs, Source/Canvas/js.rs, Source/Canvas/*.rs protocol helpers, tests/canvas.rs, tests/web_dev.rs, docs/design/frontends/canvas/NOTES.md if behavior notes drift.
- Keep /canvas and /__jet_canvas routes source-backed.

Implementation steps:
1. Replace the old palette-first left surface with a persistent Workbench-style project/file viewer backed by /canvas/project and source ids. It must show workspace/package/file/function graph navigation and source-control/provenance facts where available.
2. Keep hybrid editor modes: Code, Split, Graph. Ensure selection, source-span jump, graph picker, replay/debug overlay, inspector, and project viewer all point at the same source-backed graph state.
3. Move commands out of the palette. Add command entrypoints through right-click, Ctrl+K, and drag-from-pin release menus. Drag-release menus must filter to compatible pin/node actions and show denied actions with exact why/fix where an existing diagnostic applies.
4. Polish node language: consistent shape/color families for exec/control/data/effect/fallible/reference pins; pin label is only the variable/field name; type appears in hover/inspector detail, not default label text.
5. Render variable/const getters as compact pure capsule/bubble nodes. Allow simple variables to embed inside field/value sockets for clean graphs, with an expand action back to a normal node.
6. Add detail toggles for types, diagnostics, effects, debug values, and package metadata so the default graph is streamlined graphite/gray rather than crowded.
7. Preserve keyboard focus, reduced-motion behavior, NO_COLOR/non-visual fallbacks where terminal output is involved, and existing source transaction audit payloads.

Acceptance:
- A real Jet program opened through jet dev --target=web shows the modified hybrid Canvas UI at /canvas.
- Project/file viewer is not a command palette; commands are available through context surfaces and Ctrl+K.
- Getter capsules, embeddable variables, hover-only types, and compatible drag-from-pin menus are visible in browser proof.
- Existing graph/edit/source-control/debug features still work; no stub controls.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test canvas
- nix develop -c cargo test --test web_dev
- Browser proof against /canvas with console clean except known host warnings.
- Full nix develop -c cargo test before closing the card, unless the owner explicitly accepts scoped proof with unrelated blockers logged.

Found and reproduced a real cache-poisoning race in the current build cache (Source/BuildCache.rs + Source/CmdCompile.rs build()): cache_key() correctly SHA256-hashes the generated rust_code+profile, but the binary is compiled to a SHARED non-unique path (bin_path(file), e.g. build/main, keyed by source stem only) BEFORE store_cached(key, &bin) copies it into the content-addressed slot. Two jet processes compiling different sources with the same stem concurrently (e.g. two run/test invocations both producing build/main) can race: process A computes hash_A from its own rust_code, but by the time it calls store_cached, process B has already overwritten build/main with its binary, so hash_A permanently maps to B's binary in the shared ~/.cache/jet/build/ cache. Repro: many concurrent/rapid jet run invocations during Epoch 3 syntax-wave work; tests/cli.rs simple_exec_runs_without_a_manifest started failing (build/main.rs correct, cached binary under the correct hash printed wrong output). Fix for this card: compile to a unique per-process temp path before the content-addressed copy, so store_cached never races on a shared path. Cleared ~/.cache/jet/build/ as an immediate workaround; the poisoning will recur without the root-cause fix.

Implemented both parts.

PART 1 (race fix, section 0): BuildCache::store_cached (Source/BuildCache.rs) is now atomic -- writes to dir/bin.tmp.<pid> then fs::rename into dir/bin. CmdCompile.rs::build() no longer compiles onto the shared build/<stem> path directly: it now allocates a private per-process working dir build/.work.<bin_name>.<pid>/ holding the generated .rs, the rustc output binary, AND (discovered while writing the regression test) rustc's own crate-name-derived intermediate .rcgu.o object files, which also collided across concurrent same-stem builds and are now isolated the same way (rustc invoked with an explicit --crate-name pinned to the file stem, since the private .rs filename is not a valid crate identifier). store_cached is called against the private binary (safe: only races other processes computing the identical content-addressed key), then the private binary is fs::rename'd onto the shared build/<stem> display path (last-writer-wins on that convenience path is fine; it was never a content identity). Regression test tests/build_cache_race.rs::concurrent_distinct_sources_sharing_a_stem_do_not_poison_the_cache spawns 8 concurrent jet-run processes on distinct main.jet sources (different literal output) sharing a cwd and a JET_CACHE_DIR, then re-runs each source from its own isolated cwd against the same cache and asserts each cache hit returns exactly that source's own binary. This reproduces and pins the exact scenario the plan described (previously broke tests/cli.rs::simple_exec_runs_without_a_manifest under concurrent Epoch 3 work) and fails without the fix (verified: reproduced the crate-name and .rcgu.o collisions live before fixing them).

PART 2 (normalization, sections 1-3, D-BUILDNORM1=A): new crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs -- canonical_bytes(bundle: &ProgramBundle) serializes the WHOLE pre-sema bundle (entry file plus every module the loader resolved via imports, not just the entry) using each module's Debug-derived rendering of (pub_file, web_target_ceiling, html_path, imports, items) with a custom strip_spans() pass that removes every 'Span { start: N, end: M }' substring while leaving string/char literal contents (including ones that text-mimic a Span rendering) untouched -- verified by a dedicated unit test. Confirmed via recon (subagent read of AST.rs) that NO AST node stores comments or doc-comments (parser drops them entirely), so whitespace/comment insensitivity falls out for free from parsing + span-stripping; confirmed no HashMap/HashSet appears anywhere in the serialized item/import subtree (only in bundle-level resolved-state fields deliberately excluded, e.g. used_core/import_targets/web_partitions/dep_roots), so Debug rendering is deterministic. ast_cache_key(bundle, profile_tag, jet_version) = SHA256(canonical_bytes + 0 + profile_tag + 0 + jet_version) -- SHA-256 via the existing SHA256::sha256_hex, matching Lock::LockEnvelope::output_hash's algorithm (D-JPK-CACHE1=A interlock: same mechanism, not wired together yet, deferred to Epoch 6 as the plan directs). CanonicalAST re-exported through the full seam chain (jet-foundation -> jet-lexer/jet-parser -> jet-sema -> jet-codegen -> jet-driver -> Source/lib.rs) so Source/CmdCompile.rs can call jet::CanonicalAST::ast_cache_key.

CmdCompile.rs: new native_cache_key(file, profile_tag, mode_tag) loads the program pre-sema via Loader::load_entry_with_overlay (confirmed via recon this runs lex+parse+import-resolution only, no Sema::check_bundle), returns None (never cache) if any module's source contains embed_file/embed_bytes (external-file-bytes-not-in-AST gap, closed conservatively rather than papered over) or if the file fails to parse; folds in a SHA-256 of the enclosing pkg.jet's raw bytes (manifest_fingerprint) plus Manifest::COMPILER_VERSION as the toolchain/policy salt, so an effect-budget (D-EFFBUDGET1) tightening in pkg.jet or a compiler version bump invalidates old entries rather than being masked by an unchanged AST. jet run (mode_tag=='run', no --emit-rust) now short-circuits the ENTIRE front end on a cache hit -- sema and codegen never run, only the pre-sema parse inside the key computation -- and directly execs the cached binary. jet build deliberately keeps running its full front end even on a cache hit (only rustc is skipped, as before) because tests/pkg.rs asserts the unconditional per-build 'effects:' stderr summary and the capability summary on jet build stdout; confirmed via recon no jet-run test snapshots that stderr line, so the deeper run-side short-circuit is test-safe. jet test/doctest/bench/dev/debug builds keep their existing cache behavior (test gets its own mode_tag-scoped AST key so a test-harness binary can never be served for jet run; dev/doctest/bench/debug pass cache_key=None -- interactive/one-shot, still race-safe via build()'s private workdir). The old BuildCache::cache_key(source, profile_tag) signature is untouched and still used by BuildCache.rs's own unit tests; nothing else referenced it (checked via grep) so no call site needed updating.

SOUNDNESS ARGUMENT (I2/I3), verified end to end: a cache hit means (a) this exact whole-program AST -- entry plus every imported module, span/comment-stripped, identifier/order-sensitive -- (b) under this exact toolchain version and (c) this exact pkg.jet manifest bytes and (d) this exact build profile, was already parsed, type-checked, codegen'd, rustc-compiled to success, and (for jet run) executed at least once before. Skipping sema+codegen on a hit therefore replays a previously-validated result; it can never let unchecked code through, because storage only happens after a full successful pipeline run, and any input that could change sema's outcome for byte-identical AST bytes (imports -- closed by whole-bundle hashing; toolchain/codegen version -- closed by the version salt; manifest-driven policy like effect budgets -- closed by the manifest-fingerprint salt; embedded external file bytes -- closed by unconditionally declining to cache embed_file/embed_bytes programs) is either folded into the AST, folded into the salt, or excluded from caching outright. No gap found that required stopping; the one real external-state hazard (embed_file/embed_bytes) is handled by declining to cache rather than by hashing file bytes into the key, since Sema's own comptime_inputs tracking is only available post-sema and re-deriving it pre-sema was unnecessary when simple exclusion is sound and cheap.

TESTS: crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs #[cfg(test)] mod tests (3: strip_spans_removes_span_renderings, strip_spans_keeps_span_lookalike_inside_string_literal, strip_spans_keeps_char_literal_with_quote); tests/build_cache_normalization.rs (10: whitespace_insensitive, comment_insensitive, rename_sensitive, reorder_sensitive, profile_sensitive, version_sensitive, operator_sensitive, literal_sensitive, string_literal_content_sensitive, stable_across_reloads -- covers all six named properties plus extra discrimination guards); tests/build_cache_race.rs (1: concurrent_distinct_sources_sharing_a_stem_do_not_poison_the_cache, 8 concurrent processes). All new tests green; smoke-verified manually outside the suite too (jet run cache-miss then cache-hit shows front-end skip via -v; jet build cache-hit still prints its effects/capabilities summary).

FULL SUITE: nix develop -c cargo test --no-fail-fast run twice independently, exit 0 both times, 70/70 test binaries 'test result: ok', 0 FAILED, 1058 individual tests passed total (a one-off engine_dispatch::json_flag_forwarded_verbatim_to_engine failure on an earlier concurrent run reproduced as a PATH/binary-copy flake under full-suite parallelism -- passed alone and on both full clean reruns, unrelated to this card's files).

EXIT CRITERIA: all checked -- race fixed (store_cached atomic + build() private workdir + rename-publish); key is pre-sema canonical AST, not post-codegen Rust, with sema/codegen skipped entirely on a jet-run hit; toolchain-version salt folded in; all six normalization properties tested and passing; naming/algorithm (SHA-256, output_hash-shaped) consistent with D-JPK-CACHE1's Lock::LockEnvelope::output_hash; full suite green including the new concurrent-process regression test.

Files touched: Source/BuildCache.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs, Source/CmdDevTools.rs (two build() call sites updated for the new cache_key param), crates/jet-foundation/src/CanonicalAST.rs (new), crates/jet-foundation/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-lexer/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-parser/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-sema/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/lib.rs, crates/jet-driver/src/lib.rs, Source/lib.rs (re-export chain), tests/build_cache_normalization.rs (new), tests/build_cache_race.rs (new).

Steps: (1) Compute content hash (SHA-256, consistent with D-PKGSIGN1=B) of each package's source tree at install time; (2) Record in lock file as `content_hash: SHA256` per entry alongside version; (3) Install path becomes hash-prefixed: `.jet/store/<sha256>/<pkg>/` — deduplicates identical packages at different versions; (4) Store::verify_entry already exists (D-SUPPLY1); extend to compare stored hash vs. recomputed at each install; (5) `jet install` skips download if hash already in store (dedup); (6) Lock file format change: add `content_hash` field (backward-compatible: old lockfiles are re-resolved on next install); (7) Gated on c96 (registry) for remote packages; local path deps use hash of local tree. No new user-facing syntax. Tests in tests/ui/.

cards.plan:
U22 plan: hangar disk contract

Decision: D-JPK-GC1=B plus owner amendment is ratified. Verb is jet clean, not jet gc. Default stale_after is 30 days. Auto-GC is opportunistic and no-daemon. jet clean does GC plus optimize/dedup. Lockfile and generation reachable objects are never collected. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add reachability scan in crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Store.rs from .jet/lock package/toolchain entries and future jetos generation roots. Treat unknown legacy records as live until proven stale.
2. Extend hangar meta.json written by Store::record with last_used/realized timestamps and preserve envelope/source-state fields. Refresh last_used on cache reuse.
3. Replace current blunt Store::clean, which removes every entry. New clean computes live/stale/build-tmp classes, removes only unreferenced objects older than 30 days, sweeps orphan scratch, and keeps reachable roots.
4. Add optimize pass in jet clean: dedup or hardlink identical files inside Jet-owned hangar objects only; never mutate /nix/store outputs. Report GC bytes and optimize bytes separately.
5. Route build scratch under hangar tmp in Provider.rs / Recipe.rs / Store.rs. Clean on success and failure; U27 shell-on-fail is the later explicit preserve exception.
6. Add bounded opportunistic auto-GC after successful hangar-touching jetpack commands. No daemon, no root.
7. CLI/docs cleanup: keep jetpack clean and top-level jet clean dispatch; remove stale jet gc user text. Fix E2604 fix text in docs/spec/diagnostics.md and Source/Publish/Advisory.rs from jet gc --force to jet clean.

Likely touched: crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/Store.rs, CLI.rs, Provider.rs, Recipe.rs, Lock.rs, WorkspaceLock.rs, crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs, Source/main.rs, EngineDispatch.rs, Source/Publish/Advisory.rs, docs/spec/diagnostics.md, docs/spec/roadmap.md, tests/jetpack.rs, tests/pkg.rs, CLI transcript snapshots.

Diagnostics/tests/docs: no new diagnostic unless corrupt metadata or permission handling needs a stable code. Must update E2604 docs/fix text and any snapshot mentioning jet gc. Document 30d stale_after, live/stale/build-tmp classes, and zero-/tmp contract.

Targeted tests: old unreferenced object removed after 30d; 29d kept; lock-reachable kept regardless of age; legacy malformed metadata kept conservatively; orphan hangar tmp swept; active tmp marker kept; identical owned files dedup and report saved bytes; jetpack clean leaves live package runnable; zero-/tmp build/crash golden; jet hangar du matches on-disk bytes.

Gates: Store::clean never deletes reachable packages; no writes outside hangar/.jet in tested build paths; jet clean is only public GC verb; targeted tests then full nix develop -c cargo test --workspace green in implementation session.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: platform intent/constant CI — real tier-1 execution owned by #398/#426/#433
cards.body: Historical platform model and narrow CI test do not prove native package-manager behavior or sandboxing on macOS/Windows.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-PLATFORM1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add one canonical platform model for jetpack targets: linux, macos, windows plus arch keys used by the hangar envelope. Keep jetos Linux-only and keep Nix bridge Linux/macOS-only.
2. Thread platform keys through realization, lock/envelope records, provider selection, adapter recipes, service supervision, secrets activation, trust prompts, and diagnostics so platform-specific behavior is explicit.
3. Audit path and process handling: executable suffixes, shebang avoidance, PATH separators, case sensitivity, symlink/hardlink fallback, file permissions, shell startup, service child-process cleanup, and config/cache directories.
4. Stand up CI matrix in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` for Linux, macOS, and Windows. Keep the Nix-dependent bridge tests excluded or platform-gated on Windows; all native jetpack tests must run there.
5. Add portability fixtures for env modules, services, secrets, trust grants, adapters, hangar locks, and engine dispatch. Make every platform skip explicit and tied to D-JPK-PLATFORM1, not ad hoc.

Likely touched files/modules:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Envelope,Store,Provider,Recipe,RefSpec,Services,Secrets,Trust,Shell,CLI}.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/{Lock,Loader}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- platform fixtures under `tests/fixtures/jetpack-typed/`; tests in `tests/{jetpack,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,pkg}.rs`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add E12xx diagnostics for unsupported platform package, platform-specific bridge requirement, and non-portable adapter asset pattern if not already covered by U23.
- Update `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, `docs/spec/roadmap.md`, and epoch-4 docs only where behavior changes.
- Add CI assertions that every new diagnostic has coverage and every platform lane runs the native jetpack suite.

cards.title: Legacy substrate: no-daemon policy/status — enforced sandbox owned by #398
cards.body: Historical runtime policy detects availability and warns; it never enters an OS jail. No strong-sandbox claim remains.
cards.plan:
Decision status: D-JPK-NODAEMON1=A is ratified. No owner decision needed.

Build order:
1. Add a jetpack runtime policy module that names the invariant in code: no resident daemon, no root requirement, file-lock coordination, and sandbox downgrade policy. Keep jetos activation as the only future sudo exception.
2. Audit all jetpack verbs for daemon/root assumptions: env/dev/services/secrets/image/push/run/add/update/clean/search/info/logs/explain. Replace any implicit global state with user-owned dirs and cross-process file locks.
3. Implement or centralize hangar file locks around realization, clean/optimize, service state, secrets store writes, and discovery index writes. Tests must prove concurrent invocations serialize without corrupting lock or hangar state.
4. Add sandbox capability detection: Linux unprivileged user namespaces when present; macOS/Windows best native isolation currently available; explicit warning when downgraded. Add `jet config sandbox require` path that turns fallback into a hard error.
5. Add CI assertions for no daemon and no root: no long-lived jetpack process after verbs exit, no sudo/system service install in jetpack paths, no setuid helper, no write outside user-owned roots.
6. Thread warning/error copy through normal diagnostics and JSON output so CI can detect sandbox fallback.

Likely touched files/modules:
- New `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/RuntimePolicy.rs`, `Sandbox.rs`, or `Locking.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{Store,Services,Secrets,Trust,Shell,CLI,Provider,Recipe,WorkspaceLock}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Tests in `tests/{jetpack,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,pkg}.rs`; platform CI in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add L02xx warning for sandbox unavailable and E12xx for sandbox-required failure.
- Add E12xx for root-required invariant violation only if a runtime path can hit it; otherwise keep as CI assertion.
- Update `docs/spec/diagnostics.md`, CLI help for `jet config sandbox require`, and epoch-4 docs.
- Ensure `--json` carries sandbox status without ANSI or prose scraping.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test policy classification: jetpack verbs never require root; jetos switch is future allowlist only.
2. File-lock tests: spawn two realizes/clean/index writes against one temp hangar; assert one waits and final state parses.
3. Service tests: `jet services up/down/logs` leaves no resident jetpack supervisor after parent command exits; child services are project-local and down stops them.
4. Sandbox tests: fake capability detector for available/unavailable/require modes; assert warning vs hard error copy.
5. Path ownership tests: temp HOME/JET dirs; no writes to `/nix`, `/etc`, `/var`, global sockets, or `/tmp` except platform APIs outside jetpack control.
6. CI grep/assertion: no `sudo`, setuid helper, daemon socket, launchd/systemd install path in jetpack code or fixtures, excluding documented jetos activation code.

Gates:
- Any future design needing a daemon or privileged helper must raise a new owner decision before implementation.
- Fallback sandbox warning is loud and test-pinned; silent downgrade fails gate.
- Cross-platform behavior matches U25.
- Offline and hangar guarantees from U22/U29 remain intact under concurrent runs.

Build order:
1. Add one `NetworkMode` or `OfflineMode` value threaded through jetpack CLI dispatch, resolver, providers, adapters, cache substitution, script deps, service startup, and build runner. `--offline` must be parsed once and passed explicitly.
2. Classify verbs in code: realize-class (`env`, `dev`, `run`, `build`, `test`, `services`, package realization) versus network-class (`add`, `update`, `outdated` when refreshing, `publish`, cache push, registry sync). Network-class verbs refuse under `--offline` before doing work.
3. Teach providers and cache code to prove lock-satisfied realization from local hangar/lock only. If any object is missing and offline is set, emit one loud diagnostic naming the object/ref and the command that can fetch it later.
4. Add network-deny test harness: a fake provider/cache client that fails on network attempts plus, where practical, an env var or test hook that makes all network calls error. Prefer deterministic in-process denial over slow real network timeouts.
5. Sweep every current realize-class verb with a lock-satisfied fixture and network denied: env shell, dev with services, run package/tool, build, test, services up/health/logs, secrets activation, adapters/prebuilt/copy, images if present, discovery search/info.
6. Update docs/diagnostics and CLI help. Make `--offline` visible in completions/man output and stable JSON errors.

Likely touched files/modules:
- `crates/jet-driver/src/Jetpack/{CLI,Provider,RefSpec,Store,Recipe,ScriptDeps,ScriptLock,Services,Secrets,Trust,Image,Discovery}.rs`
- `crates/jet-driver/src/{Fetch,Lock,Loader}.rs`
- `Source/{CLI,CLISpec,EngineDispatch}.rs`, `Source/Bin/Jetpack.rs`
- Tests in `tests/{jetpack,pkg,jetpack_services,engine_dispatch,cli}.rs`; fixtures under `tests/fixtures/jetpack-typed/`

Diagnostics, tests, docs:
- Add E1258 or next free E12xx for offline-forbids-network and reuse it for fetch misses and network-class refusal, with specific What/Why/Fix per context.
- Add diagnostics.md entry and process snapshot coverage; update `jet explain` coverage through existing test.
- Document verb classification in epoch-4 docs and user CLI help.
- Ensure no ANSI, spinner, or timeout text in offline errors.

Targeted test plan:
1. Unit-test verb classification and `--offline` flag parsing through engine dispatch.
2. Lock-satisfied fixture: realize once online with fake local provider, then rerun all realize-class verbs with network denied and assert success.
3. Missing-object fixture: delete one hangar object, rerun `jet env --offline`, assert E12xx names object/ref and fix.
4. Network-class tests: `jet update --offline`, `jet add --offline`, publish/cache push under offline all refuse immediately with E12xx.
5. Adapter/build tests: locked prebuilt/copy/build recipe uses only local source and tool deps; locked `fetch(url, sha256:)` miss fails loudly under offline.
6. Service/secrets tests: offline `jet dev` starts from local hangar and decrypts local secret store without metadata refresh.
7. Discovery tests from #205: `jet search` and `jet info` read local index offline.

Gates:
- No network from realize-class verbs when lock is satisfied.
- No lazy metadata refresh, telemetry, update check, or cache probe in realize path under offline.
- Cache substitution miss falls back to local build only when not offline; under offline it errors without a fetch.
- U22 reachable-retention must keep current lock objects or this card cannot be marked done.
- Done requires golden sweep over every shipped realize-class verb, not a narrow provider unit test.

cards.title: Ship bootable jetos VM installer and install/reboot proof
cards.body: Owner acceptance: run a VM, install jetos, reboot into installed jetos, and prove it works as a real OS. Implement real QEMU boot media/disk image flow, installer environment, disk partition/format/install, bootloader or equivalent boot path, first boot into installed generation, guest-side verification, and reproducible harness. Done means a command produces media, QEMU boots it, installs to a virtual disk, reboots from that disk, then verifies packages, services, networking, generations, rollback, and proof artifacts inside the guest. The current jetos-installer-<host>.img proof text is not sufficient.
cards.plan: jetos-vm-installer

log.text: DECREE AUDIT: installer/QEMU install+reboot machinery real and keeps; caveat — kernel/initrd came from the host borrow, to be replaced by e7 #716.

Graphical proof still direct-boots verifier overlay for VNC/stdvga and checks desktop launchers. Verification: nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack; real JETOS_CACHYOS_* jetos os vm prove halcyon; nix develop -c cargo test; nix develop -c cargo fmt --check.

cards.title: Canvas full-language and Core parity truth gate
cards.body: Audit verdict: Canvas is source-backed for shipped graph/edit operations, but it does not fully edit every language feature, does not browse all Core methods, and the Run path is a debug-overlay simulation. This card owns decisions needed to turn Canvas from strong prototype into truthful full-surface editor.
cards.plan:
# Plan: Canvas full-language/Core parity gate

Ratified inputs:
- D-CANVAS-PARITY1=C AST-derived semantic ratchet plus manual UX matrix.
- D-CANVAS-CORECATALOG1=C typed Core action catalog from sema-known Core facts.
- D-CANVAS-ACTIONAUTH1=C intent cards with expert authority drawers.
- D-CANVAS-CODELENS1=C explicit Edit Source mode using source transactions.
- D-CANVAS-PROOFLENS1=C proof/debug rail with stale-proof reasons.

Implementation slices:
1. Generate Canvas parity rows from AST item/stmt/expr/type forms and current Syntax decisions; fail if a new form lacks projection/edit/support status.
2. Replace generic expr collapse where feasible with specific nodes for current core language forms; unsupported forms get explicit Canvas diagnostic/action-disabled reasons.
3. Build Core catalog endpoint from sema/Core registry: functions, methods, docs, imports, effects, fallibility, receiver type, examples, authority.
4. Wire compatible action search from pins and graph context; insertion writes ordinary Jet source and rechecks/reprojects.
5. Replace simulated Run path with real checked command/action authority for run/check/build; mutation commands require confirmation and audit payload.
6. Add explicit Edit Source mode to Code lens: edit buffer, preview diff, format/check, write/reproject, conflict detection.
7. Add proof/debug rail tied to source revision, check/build/run/proof status and stale reasons.
8. Reconcile docs/spec/spec.md, docs/reference/canvas-protocol.md, and parity matrix.

Acceptance:
- Every shipped AST language form has Canvas parity status and tests or unsupported diagnostic.
- Core method browser exposes all current Core modules/methods with typed compatible insertion.
- Split/Edit Source changes text, formats/checks, reprojects graph, and can run real output.
- Canvas Run/Build authority is real, not a toast/simulation.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test canvas
- nix develop -c cargo test --test web_dev
- Browser smoke: edit source and graph, insert Core method, run, stale proof rail updates.
- nix develop -c scripts/agent/verify-full.sh before done.

questions.text: What are the tradeoffs of option B instead of c? What is lost by going with b over c?
questions.answer: B vs C for refinements: B gives construction-checked refined values, literal checks, and flow narrowing. It does not prove arbitrary arithmetic or quantified facts. C can prove `a + b` remains PositiveInt, prove indexing is in bounds, eliminate runtime checks, and verify function postconditions over all inputs. What is lost with B: proof-preserving arithmetic, universal proofs, cross-function theorem reasoning, and check elision based on proofs. What B keeps: the most common product value, one constructor path, no solver dependency, deterministic compile times, and beginner-friendly diagnostics. Best sequencing: ship B as the surface and invariant discipline; let future C reuse those predicates if a solver/prover tier is owner-approved.

cards.title: jetos acceptance fixture: recreate the owner's ~/nixos 100% in jetos
cards.body:
The concrete dogfood proof that jetos is a drop-in NixOS replacement: the owner's real ~/nixos flake, recreated fully in jetos declarations, building and VM-boot-proving a halcyon-equivalent system.

Coverage matrix (config feature → covering card):
- flake inputs/pins/channels, per-host channel swap → jetpack U21/U30 + overlays card
- overlays/patches, NUR, allowUnfree → jetpack overlays card
- multi-variant hosts (halcyon / halcyon-plasma-beta: mkForce DM swap, tags, channel override) → module-priorities card + #326 specialisations
- disko input, btrfs → #328 declarative disks
- limine + kernel profiles + zram + sysctl + scx → kernel-tuning card (D-JOS-BOOTKERNEL1/KERNELSRC1 ratified)
- users/groups, networking (hostname, NetworkManager, nameservers, firewall ports), security (sudo, rtkit) → #262
- home-manager + per-app modules (git/ssh/fish/starship/ghostty/helix/vscode+cursor extensions/nixcord/spicetify/browsers/…) → #321 + app-module-library card
- plasma-manager/dconf-class DE settings, KDE beside GNOME default, audio, localization, xdg-mimes, fonts, virtualization (libvirt/spice), gaming (steam/wine/gamemode), smartcard → desktop-breadth card
- stylix (wallpaper/palette/fonts/cursor) → theming card
- flatpak reconcile + appimage → flatpak card
- custom ISO host → #263
- substituters → jetpack cache/providers (shipped)
- secrets → U13/#262
- jetlang packaged from local path → jetpack path providers

Exit criteria: every module file under ~/nixos has a jetos equivalent expressed in ratified syntax; the config builds; the VM test framework (#320) boots it and passes desktop-session + app-presence assertions; a written diff of anything deliberately not recreated, owner-acknowledged. Blocked by the covering cards above — this card is the ratchet that proves them done.

cards.title: jetos Studio frontend redesign — implement ratified family
cards.body: Implement the ratified jetos Studio frontend redesign as an E7 Studio slice. Build a normal clean dashboard plus sidebar app over the existing source-backed Studio projection/edit service. Dashboard is opsboard-style; settings are sidebar categories; Changeset is a first-class sidebar page; page/category registration is extensible; projectional document is not the primary UI.
cards.plan:
# Plan: jetos Studio dashboard/sidebar UI

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-STUDIO1 outcome E with owner modifications.
- D-JOS-STUDIO-HOST1: local projection/edit service plus browser fallback; no Canvas coupling.
- #264 shipped source-backed Studio prototype; this card redesigns the actual Studio UI, not semantics.

Scope:
- crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/studio_projection.rs for installed app projection.
- crates/jetpack/src/CLI/bridge_os_studio.rs, crates/jetpack/src/CLI/studio_server.rs, crates/jetpack/src/CLI/studio_transactions.rs for served/edit flows if route data needs expansion.
- tests/jetpack.rs and focused Studio tests/fixtures.

Implementation steps:
1. Replace projectional-document-first layout with a normal app shell: top status/dashboard header, left sidebar, main page, persistent staged changes footer/tray.
2. Build dashboard landing page from real data.json/source/proof facts: hosts, selected host, generation ribbon, service health, alerts, monitoring summary, proof/rollback status, and last run status. Keep copy plain and operational.
3. Build sidebar categories: Dashboard, Settings, Monitoring, Services, Packages, Secrets, Generations, Changeset, Proof/Provenance. Back categories with an internal page registry so future Studio pages register title/id/source/data needs without redesign.
4. Move settings into category pages with ordinary controls. Each setting edit must stage a source transaction and show exact Jet diff before apply.
5. Make Changeset a first-class page: unified diff, impact ledger, generation delta, proof requirements, per-hunk include where supported, Build only, Build and switch, Discard.
6. Keep one apply path. Edits from settings, dashboard alerts, rollback actions, and changeset review all stage into the same changeset/apply gate.
7. Preserve source-backed guarantees: no hidden GUI semantic state, exact config.jet diff, provenance/proof visibility, browser/headless fallback, and deterministic review output.

Acceptance:
- jetos studio --serve opens the redesigned dashboard/sidebar UI.
- Dashboard is understandable at a glance; settings are in sidebar categories; Changeset is a sidebar page.
- A settings edit previews exact Jet diff, stages in Changeset, saves through the existing transaction service, reprojects, and can run check/plan/build/proof.
- Existing #264 tests still pass and new tests cover page registry, Changeset page, dashboard data rendering, and source transaction path.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack <focused Studio tests>
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack
- nix develop -c cargo build --bin jetos
- Browser/headless proof for served Studio page.
- Full nix develop -c cargo test before done unless unrelated blockers are logged and owner accepts scoped proof.

cards.title: JetOS replacement truth gate — import real NixOS and prove installed guest
cards.body: Owner asked whether JetOS can replace an entire NixOS flake/flake-parts/Home Manager config tomorrow. Audit verdict: no. Current JetOS has substantial generation/installer/VM proof plumbing, but no full semantic NixOS/HM importer and no real installed-guest acceptance proof for the owner config. This card owns the decisions and implementation gates to make that claim true.
cards.plan:
# Plan: JetOS real NixOS replacement gate

Ratified inputs:
- D-JOS-NIXIMPORT1=C semantic NixOS/flake-parts/Home Manager importer with audited facts-only fallback.
- D-JOS-REALGUEST1=C real installed-guest proof required for replacement claims; fake QEMU only tests plumbing.
- D-JOS-DESKTOPPROOF1=C live desktop/session/app/user-home proof, not file presence.
- D-JOS-IMAGEPROOF1=C image variants are built only when bootable and smoke-proved; placeholders are staged.
- D-JOS-FIRSTBOOT1=D Studio first-boot control center with Canvas deep-link.

Implementation slices:
1. Add NixOS import IR and CLI: jet os import <flake-or-dir> --host <name> [--user <name>] [--write] [--facts-only]. Parse/evaluate available Nix facts through structured JSON, not text scraping. Generate JetOS modules for system, users, packages, services, files, secrets, overlays, specialisations, Home Manager; emit exact omissions.
2. Add fixture coverage for flake.nix, flake-parts, nixosModules, home-manager.users, overlays, mkDefault/mkForce, disabledModules, specialisations, secrets, system packages, user packages.
3. Harden jet os lift: either route to import/facts-only or downgrade wording so it cannot look like replacement import.
4. Add real-QEMU proof tier distinct from fake-tool unit tests. Fake QEMU tests remain plumbing; real acceptance rejects fake tool paths and requires guest-bound serial/display/user/app/service artifacts.
5. Upgrade desktop proof from file/script presence to live guest assertions for display manager/session, terminal fallback, Studio app, user home, browser fallback, package/service/network facts.
6. Upgrade image variants: no sparse marker says built; raw/sd/qcow only built after real artifact + smoke proof.
7. First boot: generated system launches Studio control center and proves source/proof/rollback/update health path; Canvas opens from source spans only.
8. Update docs/spec/roadmap and tests so replacement claims require import+real guest tier.

Acceptance:
- Owner-style NixOS flake/flake-parts/Home Manager fixture imports to JetOS source with zero silent omissions.
- Generated JetOS config builds offline where fixtures provide packages, and omissions are explicit otherwise.
- Real VM tier command installs, reboots, logs in, opens Studio, proves desktop/services/packages/network/home/rollback from installed disk.
- Fake-QEMU tests cannot close #363 acceptance.

Verification:

- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack os_vm_prove
- nix develop -c scripts/agent/verify-real-jetos.sh when real tier exists

cards.title: durability: formatter lossless corpus test (W2)
cards.body:
Plan: docs/plans/agent-durability.md W2. Idempotence testing provably misses dropped tokens — the exact failure mode that let jet fmt silently corrupt serde markers/turbofish for months (tests/fmt.rs:1435 admits it). Only ~3 of 94 fmt tests are byte-stability.

Scope: corpus-wide lossless check — parse(fmt(src)) token-stream-equal parse(src) for every example and every tests/ui fixture. One test closes the class; new syntax is covered automatically with no per-feature test to remember.

Exit: test in tests/fmt.rs, runs in full suite; seeded mutation check (delete a token in emission, test goes red) demonstrated in the card log.

log.text: Seeded deletion proof on final ordered oracle: temporarily changed fmt_bench to emit only '#'. Focused corpus test failed on examples/features/basics/string_view.jet at ordered token 80: before Ident("Bench"), after LParen. Mutation fully reverted; nix develop -c cargo test --test fmt then passed 98/98. Commit state clean.

criteria.text: One corpus test recursively covers every Jet example and tests/ui fixture using supported source extensions.
criteria.evidence: Sol verified complete exact manifest/accounting and recursive corpus enumeration.

criteria.text: The test compares original and formatted parsed token streams and fails on any dropped or semantically changed token while tolerating formatting-only trivia.
criteria.evidence: Sol verified ordered comparator, narrow grammar-aware normalizers, and paired negative tests; NO FINDINGS.

criteria.text: A seeded formatter token-deletion mutation is demonstrated to make the corpus test fail, then fully reverted.
criteria.evidence: Sol accepted durable mutation proof and confirmed production mutation fully absent from final commit.

cards.title: durability: tower enforcement gates (W5)
cards.body:
Plan: docs/plans/agent-durability.md W5. Today any phase jump is legal (store.mjs:224-243, triage-to-done included), decision add validates only the title, ratify outcome is unchecked against option keys, agents can write frozen/owner-lane cards, card delete cascades away ratified decisions, verdicts get mis-filed as log notes.

Scope (strictness per D-TWRGUARD1): card.checklist[] + done-gate; card.gates field required before leaving planning (BALLOT FIRST becomes structural); ballot-ready validation on decision add with --draft escape; tower verdict command minting an owner verdict as a ratified decision + card flip; ratify outcome must match an option key; owner-attribution rules for ratify/activate; non-assignee write guard; frozen/owner-lane write guard; no cascade-delete of ratified decisions; blockedBy accepts decision ids; release of a building card requires --handoff; ratify hook auto-appends syntax-decision chores (Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions.md log, jet devtools grammars, re-bless) to the card checklist.

Exit: each guard has a Tower test proving refusal/acceptance; existing board data migrates clean; skills docs updated to match.
cards.plan:
D-TWRGUARD1=C ratified — agent-hard, owner-soft. Criteria/checklist data model + done-gate + acceptance ballots are OWNED BY #463 (D-TWR-CRIT1=C); this card builds the rest of the guard family on top. All gates apply only when --by ≠ owner; owner writes bypass everything; every bypassing owner-quote is event-logged. Steps:
1. store.mjs guard layer (single chokepoint in mutate path): (a) ballot-ready validation on decision add — gist/story/inWild/options[].code/rec required, --draft flag exempts and keeps it out of the owner queue; (b) ratify/activate rejected for agents unless --quote "owner's words" given (recorded in event log); (c) no agent writes to frozen or owner-lane cards; (d) release of a building card requires --handoff note; (e) card delete refuses to cascade away ratified decisions (they retire to history instead once #461 lands; until then delete is refused outright); (f) ratify outcome must match an option key; (g) blockedBy accepts decision ids.
2. tower verdict '#N' --outcome "..." --by owner — mints an owner verdict as a ratified decision on the card and flips the card, so verdicts stop landing in logs (owner rule).
3. Ratify hook: ratifying a syntax-group decision auto-appends the standard chores (Syntax.rs, syntax-decisions.md log, jet devtools grammars, re-bless) to the card's criteria (#463 model).
4. Errors: E_GATE_* family, each with an actionable message naming the missing thing.
5. Tests: one refusal + one acceptance test per gate; owner-bypass test per gate; migration clean on live-shaped fixture.
6. Docs: Tower/AGENTS.md gate table; tower + tower-ballot skills.
Exit: every gate has paired refusal/acceptance tests; live board migrates clean; skills updated; suite green.

cards.title: Tower: archive finished board history
cards.body: tower.json is 4.2MB; 68% is closed history (496 ratified decisions = 1.7MB, 305 done cards = 1.1MB). Every write rewrites + backs up the full file (backups/ 82MB), streams it to the phone, and lands it in git (356 versions). Ballot D-TWR-ARCHIVE1 decides where finished history lives. Messages data (103KB) already removed with the messaging feature.
cards.plan:
D-TWR-ARCHIVE1=B ratified (auto-retire split live/history) MODIFIED by owner comment: keep a walk-back buffer before anything retires, and done must be strictly tested (that half lands via #463/#458). Steps:
1. store.mjs — .tower/history.json append-only ledger {decisions[], cards[], events[], each with retiredAt}. Written under the same cross-process lock; committed to git.
2. Retire policy WITH BUFFER (owner comment): on every write, retire (a) decisions status=ratified whose ratifiedAt is older than config retireAfterDays (default 3) — inside the window they stay in tower.json, show in the UI 'recently decided' strip, and tower decision reopen works one-step; (b) cards phase=done older than the same buffer AND passing the #463 done-gate rules; their questions ride along; (c) events beyond the newest 500.
3. Walk-back UX: Now view gets a collapsed 'Recently decided (N) — reversible for X days' strip listing buffered ratifications with one-tap Reopen. Reopen pulls it back to open and reverts the card advance.
4. Merged reads: findCard/decision show/card show fall through to history transparently; tower archive restore <id> moves an item back to live (reopen for ratified decisions). Board Done counts read a per-epoch summary; full done lists lazy-load via GET /api/history?epoch=.
5. CLI: tower archive status|show <id>|restore <id>. First write after upgrade migrates the existing 496 ratified decisions + 305 done cards (all outside any buffer) → tower.json ~0.5MB.
6. Tests: buffer respected (nothing retires early), reopen-from-buffer, retire-after-buffer, merged reads, restore, migration on a live-shaped fixture, backups shrink.
7. Docs: Tower README/AGENTS.md + tower-setup skill (retireAfterDays).
Exit: tower.json ≤ ~0.6MB after migration; every retired item still reachable by id; a ratification can be walked back within the buffer from phone UI; suite green.

log.text: verified by orchestrator: suite 79/79 (independent rerun); migration smoke on live-board copy: 4.2M -> 1.8M live + 2.4M history; archive status/show/restore + archived-read fallback + recentlyDecided strip working. Live retire fires on this write. Closing.

cards.title: Tower: exit criteria that gate done
cards.body: Cards have bounced (e.g. #360 twice) because done was claimable by assertion: exit criteria live in prose and nothing mechanical checks them, and owner acceptance verdicts ended up in card logs. Ballot D-TWR-CRIT1 decides the enforcement model (machine-checked criteria / acceptance ballots / hybrid flag).

D-TWR-CRIT1=C ratified — criteria list enforced everywhere + acceptance ballots on flagged cards. Steps:
1. store.mjs — card.criteria[]: {n, text, status open|met|verified, metBy, verifiedBy, evidence, at}. addCard/updateCard accept criteria; new mutations addCriterion/meetCriterion/verifyCriterion. Validation: verify rejected when verifiedBy === metBy or === assignee at meet time (E_CRITERIA_SELF).
2. Done-gate (agent-hard, owner-soft per D-TWRGUARD1=C): updateCard to phase done with --by ≠ owner rejected (E_CRITERIA) while any criterion unverified — only for cards that HAVE criteria (legacy cards unaffected). Owner writes bypass.
3. card.needsAcceptance flag (set at greenlight or any time by owner). On agent done-attempt with all criteria verified: auto-mint decision D-ACCEPT-<num> (options accept/bounce, body = per-criterion evidence summary), card stays verify; done only when owner ratifies accept; bounce comment reopens to building + log.
4. CLI: tower card criteria '#N' --add "…" | --meet n --evidence "…" --by X | --verify n --evidence "…" --by Y. tower brief (#462) includes criteria state.
5. UI: checklist w/ per-item state + evidence in card modal; acceptance ballots render in Now focus mode like any decision.
6. Tests (Tower/test): gate refusal, verifier≠builder, owner bypass, flag→mint→accept, flag→mint→bounce-reopen, legacy cards unaffected.
7. Docs: Tower/AGENTS.md, README, tower + tower-ballot skills.
