cards.title: Tower: Board view for 434 cards
cards.body: With Agents removed the UI is Now + Board. Board is an accordion wall that answers neither burndown-at-a-glance nor find-fast on phone. Ballot D-TWR-BOARD1 picks the Board archetype (roadmap ledger / ops table / spotlight search). Follow-up candidate once decided: in-app viewer for docs/plans+proposals (the old tools/Tower app had one).
cards.plan:
D-TWR-BOARD1=A ratified with comment: ADD a NEW page prototyping a hybrid of A (roadmap ledger) & B (ops table); DO NOT replace or change the current Board. Steps:
1. New third tab 'Radar' (Now · Board · Radar; keyboard 3, ⌘K entry). Board view code untouched — zero diffs to viewBoard.
2. Radar layout per epoch (active epochs only, current first): header row = name + progress bar + 30-day burndown sparkline (computed from events: card.update transitions to done, bucketed per day) + active/done counts; milestone bars with met/total and a stall badge when no progress event for 5+ days.
3. Under each epoch header: the B half — dense sortable table of that epoch's ACTIVE cards (num, title, lane, priority, order, assignee, updated-age). Column-header sort; type-to-filter box; inline edits for lane-safe fields (priority, workOrder, assignee) via existing card/update API; row click opens the normal card modal.
4. Done/frozen never render on Radar; per-epoch 'ledger' link shows done list (from tower.json now; switches to GET /api/history when #461 lands — soft dependency, not blocking).
5. Server: burndown series computed in project() (store-side helper + unit test) so the client stays dumb.
6. Tests: burndown/stall helper unit tests in Tower/test; existing suite green.
7. Acceptance (owner comment = this is a prototype he wants to SEE): card flagged for owner acceptance — demo on his phone + desktop, he compares against untouched Board, then decides keep/iterate/drop via the acceptance ballot. cards.title: corelib audit: core.process — subprocess parity with Python subprocess/Go os/exec
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Python subprocess flexibility, Go os/exec explicitness, duct-style pipelines. Current: run([cmd]) capturing everything + exit(code) only.

Gaps: streaming stdin write and incremental stdout/stderr read while the child runs; env control (set, remove, clear-then-set); working-directory control; timeout with kill; send signals (terminate/kill/interrupt); detached spawn; exit status detail (signal vs code); pipelines (child stdout → child stdin) without a shell; safe argv-only execution documented (no shell interpolation footgun — safe by default); output size limits; inherit-vs-capture per stream.

Done means: a build-tool-shaped example (spawn, stream logs live, timeout, propagate exit) ships with golden output. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan:
Acceptance: core.process must cover real build-tool and agent-operation workflows without shell strings: safe argv-only execution by default, streaming logs, exact exit status, env/cwd control, timeouts, signals, detached children, output limits, and shell-free pipelines.

Current facts found during plan pass:
- docs/reference/core-library.md documents only process.exit(code) and process.run([String]) -> ProcessResult ? IOError.
- ProcessResult currently has code/output/errors only.
- Sema/codegen know core.process exit/run only; effects classify core.process as Exec.
- Existing taint tests treat process.run as an Exec sink; any expanded surface must keep that policy coverage.

Gate queued:
- D-PROCESS1: exact process spawning/pipeline surface.

Implementation plan after gate clears:
1. Baseline tests: pin current process.run/exit behavior and taint Exec-sink coverage before expanding.
2. Data model: add ProcessSpec, Child, ExitStatus, StreamMode, ProcessPipe/Pipeline types per ratified surface. Keep argv lists canonical; no shell-string helper unless separately ratified.
3. Sema/effects: register all new calls in CheckerCoreLib known-items, mark Exec effects, preserve taint sink checks on every execution path, and type-check stream/stdin/stdout modes.
4. Runtime/codegen: implement through TIR/prelude only; no codegen checks. Use std::process Command internally; map OS errors into IOError and child outcomes into ExitStatus without exposing Rust/stdout internals.
5. Safety defaults: bounded capture default or explicit output_limit, no inherited env mutation, timeout kill semantics documented, process handles RAII-clean where possible, and interrupt/terminate/kill behavior platform-pinned.
6. Examples/goldens: build_runner.jet streams stdout, sets cwd/env, times out a child, pipelines two argv commands, propagates exit. Keep fixture commands cross-platform or test-gated.
7. Docs: update docs/reference/core-library.md, docs/spec/spec.md effects table, syntax-decisions D-PROCESS1 entry, and stdlib ledger (#310 if present).
8. Verification: targeted process/taint/golden tests, cargo build, hello smoke, process example smoke, final nix develop -c cargo test before close.

Devil-pass hardening:
- No shell string default; argv-only is the safe path.
- No silent output buffering footgun; streaming and capture limits are explicit.
- No second process model; process.run lowers to ProcessSpec.run.
- No raw OS status leaks; ExitStatus is typed and portable.

cards.plan:
# Plan: jet dev server pinned dashboard + overlay

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-DEVSRV1 outcome D with owner modification: keep a nicely formatted pinned terminal dashboard header.

Scope:
- Source/CmdDevWeb.rs for dev web server output and injected browser overlay/status strip.
- tests/web_dev.rs and any dev-server CLI transcript tests.

Implementation steps:
1. Add terminal dashboard header for TTY: status, URL/port, watched target, client count, last build time, current build/error state. Header remains pinned while logs scroll below.
2. Keep one shared poll/status source for browser strip and terminal header so ready/building/error/offline/client count cannot drift.
3. Browser corner strip mirrors status; on error it expands to full overlay with verbatim diagnostic frame over last-good build.
4. Terminal verbose mode/request log prints under the same header. Errors erase/settle any live region before printing diagnostics.
5. Non-TTY output degrades to append-only deterministic status lines. NO_COLOR uses words instead of color-only state.
6. Preserve current dev server routes, last-good-build behavior, Canvas route, and reload/poll protocol.

Acceptance:
- jet dev <file> --target=web shows pinned dashboard header in TTY.
- Browser strip and terminal header report identical state and client count.
- Compile error shows full browser overlay and terminal diagnostic; clean rebuild clears both.
- Request/rebuild logs appear below the header.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test web_dev
- Add/update focused tests for status payload, overlay injection, terminal formatting fallback, and non-TTY output.
- Browser smoke: launch jet dev, load app and /canvas if relevant, trigger compile error, verify overlay clears after fix.

Registry/signing ops (publish, keygen, key, yank, vendor — Source/CmdSupply.rs) and introspection ops (semindex, dossier, impact, graph, query, codemod, expand, audit, sbom) live directly in the Source/ root crate, not crates/jetpack — a verb-ownership question #367/D-PRODUCT-SPLIT1 (binary/crate ownership) did not address. jet ? cards.title: Sema soundness audit: adversarial review + fuzz corpus expansion
cards.body:
jet-sema (~40k lines) owns all checking (I3); a soundness hole means unsound generated Rust reaches users silently — the worst bug class in the project (I1/I2). #185 (done) swept reachable ICEs and rustc leaks; this card hunts the other two classes: accepts-invalid (sema approves a program it must reject) and miscompiles (approved program computes the wrong thing).

Audit surface, in priority order:
1. Ownership/move/borrow proofs, including the tier-2 view/ref rules (E2-M5) and RAII cleanup (S63).
2. Sendability proofs for tasks/channels (E2-M1) — data-race freedom claims.
3. #Unsafe gate containment (D-LL1): generated `unsafe` appears only inside user-written gates; safe Jet emits none (tests/golden.rs enforces — extend it).
4. Generics + trait resolution: associated types, error conversion for `?`, trait delegation (S62), argument labels/defaults (S61).
5. Comptime/@Pure evaluation boundary (M9.5, E2-M16) — comptime results must agree with runtime semantics.
6. Newer surface: fan-out `f.[…]` (S75), fixed-size lists `[T#N]` (S76), refinements (D-REFINE1 when landed).

Method: adversarial review pass per area → each suspected hole becomes a tests/ui fixture or golden test BEFORE the fix; extend tests/fuzz_sema.rs with generative/mutation strategies over the ratified grammar; use the interpreter-vs-compiled differential battery (I2, jet dev parity) as a miscompile oracle — divergence is always a bug in one side.

Done means: audit notes committed under docs/ (findings, per-area verdict, corpus description); every confirmed hole has a failing test then a fix, all suite green; fuzz corpus + runner wired so #211 CI can execute it in budget; no invariant bent. No owner gates expected — if a finding requires a semantics change visible to users, ballot it before fixing.
cards.plan: Order: (1) read docs/spec/architecture.md R1–R12 + spec.md sections per area; (2) per audit area, spawn adversarial review (opus-tier reasoning) over the relevant sema modules — CheckerCore.rs, CheckerInfer/, CheckerCoreLib.rs, Bundle.rs; (3) write attack programs as tests/ui fixtures — expect reject; write miscompile candidates as differential fixtures — expect byte-identical interpreter/compiled output; (4) extend tests/fuzz_sema.rs: grammar-directed generation from crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs so the fuzzer only speaks ratified syntax; (5) fix confirmed holes smallest-first, full suite between fixes; (6) audit notes + corpus docs; full nix develop -c cargo test green at close.

cards.title: jetpack/jetos CLI output redesign — implement ratified family
cards.body: Implement the ratified hybrid jetpack/jetos CLI output as an E4 output substrate slice. Keep colored + - ~ plan symbols, support both -y and --yes, and add nh-style dependency chain/progress visualization for long downloads/builds/realization where appropriate. Jetos uses the same output substrate later.
cards.plan:
# Plan: jetpack/jetos hybrid CLI output

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-CLI1 outcome D with owner modifications: keep colored + - ~; both -y and --yes; add nh-style dependency chain/graph visualization for long builds/downloads.

Scope:
- crates/jetpack/src/Output.rs, crates/jetpack/src/CLI/*.rs command call sites, crates/jetpack/src/JetOS/commands.rs and generation/proof call sites that already share Theme/Output.
- tests/jetpack.rs, CLI usage tests, fixture stderr/stdout snapshots where output is pinned.

Implementation steps:
1. Extend the shared Theme/Output layer with consequence-scaled rendering: quiet ledger, pinned live region for long work, plan gate for mutations, deterministic plain fallback.
2. Preserve colored +, -, ~ for plan diffs; NO_COLOR replaces color with stable text markers while keeping symbols readable.
3. Normalize confirmation bypass so -y and --yes are accepted everywhere the mutation confirmation gate appears. Non-TTY mutation without yes prints plan and exits without applying.
4. Add dependency-chain progress model for long realization/build phases: downloads, builds, cached/reused nodes, current edge, counts, size/elapsed where known. Render as a pinned graph/chain in TTY; append ledger lines in non-TTY.
5. Wire jetpack add/build/env/gc and jetos plan/build/switch/proof through the same output primitives where they already share command execution paths.
6. Erase live regions before diagnostics; diagnostics remain verbatim.
7. Keep JSON output schemas untouched unless a separate schema version decision is raised.

Acceptance:
- Trivial commands stay quiet.
- Long build/download commands show useful dependency-chain progress in TTY.
- Mutations show a plan with + - ~ and require confirmation unless -y/--yes.
- Non-TTY output is deterministic and non-interactive.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack <focused CLI output tests>
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack
- Add transcript/snapshot coverage for + - ~, -y, --yes, non-TTY no-hang, NO_COLOR, and dependency-chain fallback.
- Full nix develop -c cargo test before done.

cards.title: jet env shell prompt — implement ratified family
cards.body: Implement the ratified hybrid jet env shell prompt as an E4 jetpack environment slice after the prompt config follow-up decision clears. Default prompt shows env name plus partial path. Keep adaptive status, transient receipts, ^G glance, and optional status strip without making shell state a second source of truth.
cards.plan:
# Plan: jet env hybrid prompt

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-PROMPT1 outcome D with owner modification: show env name and partial path by default.

Blocking decision raised by this plan:
- D-FE-PROMPT-STRIP1 chooses the user-facing config surface for the optional always-on status strip.

Scope after decision clears:
- crates/jetpack/src/Shell.rs for bash/zsh/fish rc generation.
- crates/jetpack/src/CLI/run_enter_dev.rs and ModuleEval env config types only if prompt config schema changes.
- tests/jetpack.rs, tests/env_dev_trust.rs, and focused shell rc tests.

Implementation steps:
1. Make default prompt include environment label and compact current path in bash, zsh, and fish. Keep current dev-shell branding unmistakable.
2. Add adaptive receipt/status behavior where feasible in shell rc: transient command receipt, running marker for Jet-owned commands, failure next-action line without restating diagnostics.
3. Implement ^G glance for build/test/env status if supported by the generated shell rc; unsupported shells get a documented no-op fallback rather than broken control sequences.
4. Implement optional always-on strip exactly as the ratified D-FE-PROMPT-STRIP1 config says.
5. Respect NO_COLOR/CLICOLOR and non-TTY shell startup. No powerline-only glyph dependency; words carry the state.
6. Keep env source truth in env.jet/module eval; no hidden prompt database.

Acceptance:
- Entering jet env in bash/zsh/fish shows env name and partial path by default.
- NO_COLOR renders readable words without ANSI reliance.
- Optional strip can be enabled by the ratified config and shows the same status words as ^G.
- Existing trust/env behavior and foreign flake fallback remain unchanged.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack <focused env/shell tests>
- nix develop -c cargo test --test env_dev_trust
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack
- Manual spawned-shell smoke for generated bash/zsh/fish rc where available.
- Full nix develop -c cargo test before done.

questions.text: I want to use add but we need to have two methods available. One that adds and overwrites on collision and one that does not overwrite on collision. Propose updated methods so experts can control whether they want to have values be updated by default if key already exists or if they want to add unique, only if the key is new
questions.answer: Ballot updated to your direction. Option A (rec) is now: one verb family — add(key, value) -> T? upserts and returns the displaced old value (None = the key was fresh), so the default path already gives experts collision visibility for free; add_new(key, value) -> Bool stores only if the key is absent and returns false with the existing value untouched — the race-safe claim in one call. Element containers: add(value) -> Bool. insert and put both die; scores[name] = v index-write stays the literal upsert. Precedents: Rust insert returning Option<old>, .NET indexer + TryAdd.

cards.title: Tower: server restarts on code change (or version-mismatch banner) — stale-process trap

criteria.text: restart-loop guard: if the newly spawned process crashes within the 2s window, the old process falls back to reopening its own server instead of retrying — verified by test/restart.test.mjs
criteria.evidence: Code-level (per orchestrator instruction, live/scratch restart-loop repro not required): Tower/app/restart.mjs read in full. cards.title: dev suite parallel flake: core.perf fidelity signal is a process-global static
cards.body: Under full parallel cargo test --test dev, core.perf fidelity signal races across JIT-resident test threads: cranelift_three_way_differential_battery diverges on tooling/fidelity and 3+ sibling tests sharing dev_diff_lock cascade with PoisonError. Green standalone/single-threaded. Architectural: the signal needs per-instance or thread-scoped state (or the battery needs an isolation harness). Observed across waves on card 521 (2026-07-12/13).

log.text: Fidelity signal statics converted to thread_local (c06b735f): jit runtime_host + comptime Methods; AOT static untouched (per-process naturally). dev target 57/57 at default parallelism twice + serialized once; golden/effects clean. 3/3 criteria met+verified (jet-verify-close3).

Root cause: core.perf fidelity signal was process-global (static AtomicU32) in both in-process tiers -- jet-jit resident JIT (runtime_host.rs JIT_PERF_FIDELITY) and jet-comptime interpreter/REPL (Methods.rs PERF_FIDELITY) -- shared by every cargo-test thread in the one test binary process. AOT tier's own static (jet-codegen Prelude/Core.rs) is correctly untouched: each AOT run is a separate OS process already. Fix: both in-process statics -> thread_local Cell<u32> (not per-JitRuntime-instance: resident_jit_fidelity_matches_runtime_contract's ?-early-return design needs fidelity to survive a full try_compile_bundle teardown+fresh_runtime restart on the SAME thread, ruling out scoping to JitRuntime/Interp). thread_local isolates concurrent test threads (fixes the race + PoisonError cascade via dev_diff_lock) while preserving same-thread persistence across restarts/hot-swaps/REPL turns. Evidence: cargo test --test dev default-parallel 3 consecutive clean runs (55/55, excluding 2 pre-existing tests that fail identically on unmodified master, parallel or solo: jit_coverage_audit/jit_try_compile_manifest_matches, a JIT-gap-manifest drift unrelated to this bug); --test-threads=1 55/55; cranelift_three_way_differential_battery + resident_jit_fidelity_matches_runtime_contract + interpreter_matches_compiled_binary + dev_default_matches_compiled_binary all green standalone; golden 3/3, effects 48/48; jet run smoke ok. cards.title: JIT tier-1a: Cranelift JIT (dev-loop hot-reload) — c139
cards.body: Ideas.md: add Cranelift JIT, later own bytecode/native JIT. Was Tower c139 (ready); c140/c141 (own bytecode VM / own native JIT) are separate frozen v2 cards. Jet is AOT-compiled; the Cranelift JIT is the optional hot-reload dev accelerator (tier-1 over interpreter tier-0), not how the language runs. Accepted work. Bundle-risk: Cranelift JIT vs later custom tiers differ. Owner requirement (2026-06-30): JIT and `jet run` must be functionally identical on every program the AOT path covers; native stays the performance tier. `jit_covers` must converge on `tir_covers`, not fall back to the E2201 interpreter for tasks/channels/Core.
cards.plan: JIT/AOT parity by construction. Canonical plan: docs/plans/epoch-3/jit-aot-parity.md. Orchestration: implementation agent must first read .agents/prompts/OrchestrationPrompt.md and run as that orchestrator. Owner direction 2026-07-06: Jet wins two fronts. AOT targets C/C++/Rust/Go/Zig/Odin territory with optimized native binaries and expert control; JIT/dev targets JS/TS/Python/data-analysis/web-dev loops with rapid design/test/refine. Every AOT-runnable program must run under jet dev in some backend path with identical stdout/stderr/exit/diagnostics/panics/side effects. Native JIT lowering is preferred for speed; transparent shared-runtime/platform/AOT-subprocess fallback is valid when resident JIT hosting is unsafe or incomplete. User never owns backend gaps. No parity ballots remain. Exit: dev_default_matches_compiled_binary covers stdout+stderr+exit for every example, gap manifest contains only transparent internal fallback reasons, no jit_covers whitelist remains, R12 documents two consumers/one IR, full suite + jet-verify green.

questions.text: Give me the tradeoffs, limitations, and benefits that we would get from having both A & B as the selected option
questions.answer: Having both A ($ splice source fragments) and B (typed AST builder API) simultaneously: BENEFITS — (1) $ splice covers quick, copy-modify derives (easy to read, errors in Jet source terms); (2) AST builder covers programmatic generation without string concatenation or escaping; (3) users can pick the right tool for their derive's complexity. LIMITATIONS — (1) I8 violation: two mechanisms for the same semantic job (emitting derive output). Real codebases will use both; code review becomes harder. (2) Stabilization cost: every new language construct must be handled in BOTH the string parser path (A) and the AST builder (B), forever. Miss one and the two systems diverge. (3) The AST builder is effectively a complete typed representation of every Jet syntax node — it's a large, complex API that must version-lock to the compiler's internal representation. (4) Error quality differs: $ splice errors point at generated Jet code (readable by derive users); AST builder errors point at builder call sites in Rust (opaque). VERDICT: the costs outweigh the benefits. Teams will converge on one; having both means maintaining two. Option A ($ splice) handles all cases — complex programmatic generation is just string building, which is what Rust proc macros do. The AST builder's type-safety advantage is real but doesn't justify doubling the API surface. Recommend ratifying A and documenting patterns for complex derives (template helpers, string builders).

cards.title: REPL frontend redesign — implement ratified family
cards.body: Implement the ratified hybrid REPL frontend redesign in Source/REPL.rs after its follow-up owner gates clear. Keep the line REPL foundation, layered completion/docs/bindings depth, and notebook-style controls for addressable turns: rerun, fold, unfold, and pin.
cards.plan:
# Plan: hybrid REPL with notebook controls

Ratified inputs:
- D-FE-REPL1 outcome D, with explicit owner request for notebook-style rerun/fold/unfold/pin controls.

Blocking decisions raised by this plan:
- D-FE-REPL-DOCS1 chooses the ?name docs surface.
- D-FE-REPL-RERUN1 chooses rerun/downstream semantics.

Scope after decisions clear:
- Source/REPL.rs, tests/repl.rs, tests/repl/*.txt, tests/cli/no_args_repl_banner.txt if banner/prompt output changes.
- No diagnostic wording changes unless a new diagnostic is separately registered and snapshotted.

Implementation steps:
1. Preserve current REPL semantics and transcript compatibility as the floor. Non-TTY and NO_COLOR keep plain line transcripts.
2. Add turn ids to interactive TTY output. Each turn stores input, output summary, status, duration when available, folded state, pin state, and binding changes.
3. Add controls: rerun, fold, unfold, pin/unpin. Controls must have keyboard commands and textual fallbacks, not icon-only behavior.
4. Add pinned value/turn area that stays visible without changing evaluation semantics.
5. Add folded output rendering for long values/errors and unfold in place.
6. Implement docs and rerun behavior exactly per the ratified follow-up decisions.
7. Keep diagnostics verbatim; frame/styling may change, words/codes may not.

Acceptance:
- Interactive REPL shows addressable turns with notebook controls.
- Pin/fold/unfold/rerun work in TTY mode and degrade cleanly in plain transcripts.
- Large output folds without losing data.
- Bindings remain truthful after rerun according to the ratified rerun policy.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo test --test repl
- nix develop -c cargo test --test diagnostic_snapshots ui_snapshots -- --exact if any diagnostic frame fixture changes
- nix develop -c cargo test --test cli question_mark_help -- --exact if CLI startup/help paths are touched
- Full nix develop -c cargo test before done.

cards.title: Prepare clean jet / jetpack / jetos product split
cards.body: Audit found process split but not crate/product split: root package still builds jetpack/jetos, jetos is a jetpack os wrapper, driver depends on jetpack, tests are mixed. This card prepares split boundaries without changing user semantics until owner decides visible ownership.
cards.plan:
# Plan: Prepare clean jet / jetpack / jetos split

Ratified input:
- D-PRODUCT-SPLIT1=C canonical ownership split with teaching/provenance shims.

Implementation slices:
1. Extract shared package/config model crate for read-only manifest/lock/store/ref/workspace/script data so jet-driver no longer depends on jetpack engine.
2. Move jetpack binary ownership into crates/jetpack; create real crates/jetos binary/crate for OS workflows.
3. Keep jet root focused on language/compiler/dev loop; route compatibility forms with clear owner/provenance messages.
4. Split ModuleEval plan model from env runtime and JetOS realization.
5. Move Canvas package/workspace scans behind shared model API.
6. Split tests/jetpack.rs into package engine, dispatch, JetOS generation/proof, Studio, and fixture helpers.
7. Update workspace dependency guards and docs paths.

Acceptance:
- Root package owns only jet; jetpack/jetos binaries come from owning crates.
- jet-driver no longer depends on jetpack engine.
- Existing public commands remain byte-compatible or emit ratified teaching/provenance messages.
- Canvas project scan works through shared model.

Verification:
- nix develop -c cargo check --workspace
- nix develop -c cargo test --test workspace_crates
- nix develop -c cargo test --test engine_dispatch
- nix develop -c cargo test --test jetpack
- nix develop -c scripts/agent/verify-full.sh before done.

cards.title: Concurrency runtime push: Go-scale M:N tasks + structured combinators
cards.body: Canonical Epoch 3 concurrency push. Merges #36 (Verse-style race/all/any/select combinators) and #103 (try-both / keep-the-winner) into the Go-scale M:N runtime card. Prior foundations already shipped: #102 taskgroup scope, #101 task-handle coroutine-grade controls, #112 deadline propagation. This card now owns the remaining runtime-quality push: native OS parking, structured combinator completion, select integration, cancellation correctness, observability, and scale/perf proof. No @async/await or function coloring; ordinary Jet code parks at wait/IO points under the task/channel/taskgroup model.
cards.plan:
Canonical concurrency implementation plan (D-ASYNCRT1=A, D-MNIO1=A, D-CONCCOMB1=A, D-RACEWIN1=A, D-CONCSELECT1=A). Build one model only: task/channel/taskgroup. No @async/await, no user coroutine primitive, no second race/select mechanism.

Already shipped foundations to preserve:
- #102: taskgroup g { ... }, g.task { ... }, wait/join, scope-exit ownership, existing g.all/g.race/g.any vertical slice.
- #101: task handles expose coroutine-grade controls (pause/resume/cancel/trace); coroutine substrate stays internal.
- #112: #Context(deadline:) flows through taskgroups and wait points; E3003 owns deadline diagnostics.
- #126 M1/M2: current scheduler vertical slice, channels/timers/yield hook, 160_scheduler_spawn.

Implementation order for dumb agents:
1. Inventory current behavior first. Read docs/spec/philosophy.md, syntax-decisions.md entries for D-ASYNCRT1/D-MNIO1/D-NURSERY1/D-TASKSCOPE1/D-CONCCOMB1/D-RACEWIN1/D-CONCSELECT1/D-DEADLINE1/D-COROUTINE1, docs/plans/epoch-3/concurrency-vision.md, Source/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, Source/Interpreter.rs, crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Scheduler.rs, task/channel sema/codegen, and tests for examples 131, 157, 158, 160.
2. Write missing acceptance tests before code. Add/extend examples/features concurrency examples plus CLI/golden tests for: 100k idle parked tasks or smallest CI-safe equivalent with a scale benchmark guard; channel receive wakes one parked task without busy-wait; taskgroup scope cancels losing race tasks; g.all fail-fast cancels siblings; g.race returns first success and cancels losers; g.any returns first completion including errors; if g.select() arms deregister losers; deadline firing wakes parked I/O/channel/task waits with Jet-owned E3003; detached tasks require explicit expert policy/name.
3. Replace cooperative-only scheduler gaps with real parker abstraction. Define internal runtime traits, not user syntax: Scheduler, Parker, TimerWheel, IoParker. Start with portable readiness fallback for tests; implement D-MNIO1 native backends behind cfg modules (Linux epoll/io_uring path, macOS/BSD kqueue, Windows IOCP). No external runtime dependency unless owner approves a new dep card.
4. Route every blocking-looking stdlib wait through the parker. Channel recv/send, timers/sleep, task join/wait, TCP accept/read/write, HTTP client/server waits must park Jet tasks, not OS threads. Real OS-blocking fallback must run on an explicit blocking pool and be observable; never silently block scheduler workers.
5. Finish structured combinators in taskgroup only. g.all/g.race/g.any/select are methods or scoped operations on the taskgroup; they create no detached work and return/propagate through one cancellation model. Implement D-RACEWIN1 inside g.race; #103 is merged here. Implement D-CONCCOMB1 here; #36 is merged here.

Diagnostics/lints: forgotten task handle wait, swallowed cancellation, deadline ignored, detached task without policy/name, real blocking call on scheduler worker.

Prove parity and scale. cargo test green; examples 131/157/158/160 still pass; add deterministic scheduler tests with fake clock; add stress tests gated for CI budget; add a benchmark/report target that demonstrates 100k parked connections/tasks when run locally. rustc errors remain ICE-only; all user errors are sema/driver diagnostics.

questions.text: What is the best of both worlds approach here? We are trying to provide best in class service & support for any use case, not just some.
questions.answer: Best of both worlds for async is M:N green threads (Option A) — here's why it delivers everything: (1) No function coloring. Beginners write `task { do_io() }` and experts write the same thing. There is no async/non-async split to manage. Go demonstrates this at Internet scale. Java added Project Loom (virtual threads) specifically because async/await (Option B) proved inadequate — the industry has already run this experiment. (2) High concurrency for free. An M:N scheduler parks threads on IO waits and runs other tasks, achieving 100k+ connections without any new syntax. (3) Expert control is still available: task handles give you priorities, pinning, cancellation, monitoring. Channels give you explicit synchronization. These are the expert levers, just not a second concurrency MODEL. Why not Option C (hybrid M:N + @async)? I8: having two yielding mechanisms (green-thread park and @async fn future) is two ways to write concurrent code. Teams standardize on one and the other becomes dead weight or, worse, they mix and no one can read the code. The apparent limitation of Option A — 'I can't explicitly control when I yield' — is the Go objection, and Go's answer is: you don't need to. Task/channel primitives cover all real expert needs. Recommendation: Option A. It IS the best of both — simplicity without sacrificing power.

questions.text: For all/most of the “marker/attributes”, or at least the ones for which this is appropriate like memory, why not have the ability to mark individual scopes/blocks, functions, modules, AND packages. This way the user can define in one place based on where they want the given “marker” to be relevant insteead of tons of repetition. This also keeps consistency throughout various echelons. Please update this ballot accordingly and open another ballot/card to allow that type of scoping everywhere as appropriate
questions.answer:
Yes. Adopt one scoping ladder for eligible markers: block, function, module, and package. One declaration applies below that point; the innermost declaration of the same marker key wins, while unrelated inherited keys remain. `jet explain` should show the effective value and every contributing or overridden declaration.

Memory facts are eligible: `#Policy(no_alloc)`, `zero_rc`, and `arena_bounded(N)`. Effect bounds and prohibitions can inherit where their semantics remain sound. `#Unsafe` needs split treatment: block and function forms may authorize audited unsafe operations, while module and package forms may only tighten policy, such as forbidding unsafe code or requiring audit evidence. A wide `#Unsafe` authorization would violate the user-written audited-region requirement.

Keep per-site claims narrow when the proof depends on the exact site. `#Grant` creates a lexical authority handle that must not escape. `#Tainted` marks a specific value origin. `#Sanitizer` vouches for one function. Serde field attributes change one field's wire shape. Those cannot safely become implicit package-wide claims.

questions.text: This seems excessive if it is the default requirement. We want to treat experts like adults, not baby them. If we need to enforce stricter rules, then that should be enforceable and auditable for enterprises/teams, but should not be forced for EVERY user unless they opt in and need the safety. We need to allow ignoring/bypassing things like unsafe as opt in at package level. That way if a new user (who is an expert) wants to do some unsafe work, they can just use a single flag or add a single line to the package file to suppress/ignore/ skip need for unsafe markings
questions.answer:
You're right about the additional typed obligation layer. I reworked option A so normal packages keep the current D-LL1/D-UNSAFE2 behavior: the `#Unsafe` gate alone. Teams opt into `policy: { unsafe: .Obligations }`; audit output records the effective policy and each operation's obligations. Experts can write `policy: { unsafe: .Relaxed }` once, which makes the reason optional and removes L3101, but still requires a `#Unsafe` region or function for low-level operations.

Boundary: under current I1 and D-UNSAFE2, no package setting may permit raw operations outside `#Unsafe`. Memory and type safety remain enforced outside every gate.

Your request to “skip need for unsafe markings” could instead mean removing `#Unsafe` itself. That conflicts with current I1 and D-UNSAFE2 and requires an explicit invariant-amendment ballot. I added that as separate option D: `policy: { unsafe: .Unchecked }` permits package-wide ungated unsafe and records that choice. I recommend A: adult default, optional enterprise obligations, one-line reduced ceremony, and the ratified boundary intact.

questions.text: My idea for opt in GC is that it could be supported as a package level setting or potentially smaller scope depending on user config. This way for things like go-project replacements in jet or typescript or python project replacements, the user could just opt into using the GC once and not worry about it. We should allow finer control and open up the GC to be usable on a lower mechanical level for embedding into modules/functions/etc, but should be magic by default. Also I want it to have a logging capability which could serve as a way to track/tool/debug where memory isn’t properly traced so that we have a clear way for the user to remove the GC and be fully borrow checker based. Update this card accordingly and make a new set of cards/ballots as needed to meet this goal
questions.answer:
Yes. The updated ballot proposes GC opt-in on the four-echelon ladder being opened by D-MARK-SCOPE1 from #644. One `package.jet` line can cover a whole Go, TypeScript, or Python replacement. The same setting can narrow to a module, function, or block.

Under the recommended option, GC is magic inside an opted scope. Heap values gain traced identity with no `Gc<T>` ceremony. Bare storage creates a traced edge; `&` still gates writes, `^` transfers a root, and `~` stays a deep copy. Outside the scope, D-MEM1 remains unchanged.

GC observability is also a required migration path. Trace mode records every allocation the ownership checker could not prove, its source site, and the reason. `jet gc report` groups those sites and gives concrete fixes, such as owned restructuring or `Pool<T>`/`Id<T>`. The target end state is an empty report, after which the scope opt-in can be removed.

D-DEP-GC1=A already chose the std-only native collector, so this does not reopen I6. Any later external collector or runtime bridge needs its own I6 ballot. Two implementation cards cover scope semantics and trace/report tooling.

cards.title: GC scope opt-in: package, module, function, block
cards.body: Implement D-OPTGC1's `gc` key in the existing `#Policy(…)` family across package, module, function, and block scope through D-MARK-SCOPE1's shared applicability matrix. Do not build GC-specific inheritance. A package opt-in gives Go, TypeScript, and Python replacement projects automatic traced storage without `Gc<T>` ceremony. Narrower scopes support embedded GC subsystems. D-MEM1 read, `&` write, `^` take, and second-class-borrow safety remain enforced. Outside opted scopes, ownership stays the default. This card owns GC semantics, sema, TIR, AOT, dev parity, diagnostics, docs, and examples. GC trace/report behavior is tracked separately.
cards.plan: After #646 supplies the private collector and #657 supplies the common policy ladder, implement D-OPTGC1=A's frontend semantics only. Register package `policy: .{ gc: true }` and post-D-SHAPE2 narrower `@Policy(gc)` through the shared matrix. Within the effective scope, sema automatically promotes eligible heap graphs to traced identity while preserving bare read, `&` write, `^` take/root transfer, and `~` deep copy; reject unproven escape into ownership-only code with effective-scope provenance. Retire the public `core.gc`/`Gc<T>` wrapper surface and migrate examples/docs so scoped promotion is the sole source path. TIR/AOT/dev route promoted graphs through #646's private collector. This card does not implement tracing or `jet gc report`; #659 owns observability.

cards.title: GC trace and report: migration back to ownership
cards.body: Implement D-OPTGC1 observability as a supported GC-to-ownership migration workflow. Trace mode records every allocation the ownership checker could not prove, its source span, effective GC scope, reason, and runtime counts. `jet gc report` groups those sites and gives concrete fixes that remove traced storage. Human and JSON output support local debugging, CI trend tracking, and a clear empty-report gate before removing `#Policy(gc)`. This command is memory analysis; `jet clean` remains Hangar cleanup.
cards.plan: After #658 establishes the sole scoped-GC frontend path, add observability only. Tracing is explicit and zero-cost when off. Prove malformed/stale trace rejection, AOT/dev equivalence, cyclic examples, migration rewrites, and the empty-report removal gate. #646 remains collector owner and #658 remains scope/promotion owner.

cards.title: core.auth base64url decoder accepts non-canonical encodings (JWS signature malleability)
cards.body: Found via full-suite flake (core_auth_verify_jwt_bad_signature_is_error fails ~25-50% of runs): jet_auth_b64url_decode (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/CoreLib/Top/Auth.rs) ignores nonzero trailing padding bits, so a signature whose final base64url char is altered within the padding band decodes to the same 32 bytes and verifies. RFC 7515 requires rejecting non-canonical base64url exactly to prevent this malleability. Fix fail-closed: decoder rejects nonzero leftover bits; verify_jwt maps signature-part decode failure to InvalidSignature. Related same-day flake to diagnose: tests/pkg.rs key_rotation_warns_not_errors intermittently reds with E1246 (signature doesn't match recorded public key) — determine whether it shares the canonicality bug or is a distinct signing-path nondeterminism; card separately if distinct. Prelude is include_str-embedded: rebuild jet before smoke tests.
cards.plan: Fix canonicality once in shared `jet_auth_b64url_decode`: reject impossible residual lengths and any nonzero unused trailing bits before returning bytes, while preserving the accepted URL alphabet and unpadded canonical form. Audit every decoder caller so stricter rejection is intentional. In JWT verification, map signature-segment decode/canonicality failure to InvalidSignature without changing header or payload error contracts. Add exhaustive last-character alias regressions for both padding-bit widths, canonical RFC vectors, malformed alphabet/length cases, and an end-to-end token whose altered signature text formerly verified. Rebuild the include_str-embedded prelude before smoke tests. Reproduce the key_rotation flake independently; if it survives this fix, raise a separate root-cause card rather than folding unrelated signing nondeterminism into this patch.

cards.title: Allow user definition of operators for classes/structs - even python does this
cards.body: Allow user definition of operators for classes/structs - even python does this. We should have excellent, convenient, and intuitive default behavior but allow full access to “internal” apis, like operator definitions for structs/types. Need to design and choose a consistent syntax. Python uses double underscore prefix (and postfix?) to indicate some of these.
cards.plan: Implement D-OPDEF1 through the existing capability mechanism, not Python-style dunder names or a second operator registry. Reuse closed capability bundles such as @Numeric/@Comparable: parse and register the ratified declaration form, resolve exactly one operator method per type, type-check same-type/result laws in sema, lower approved calls through TIR, and keep codegen inference-free. Preserve E0105 no-overload and built-in lane/linalg closure. Ship Money/Vec-style examples plus ambiguity, missing capability, wrong operand/result, orphan, and recursion diagnostics.

cards.title: Terminal + CLI visual system: designed color/polish on EVERY user-facing surface
cards.body:
Owner mandate (repeated, 2026-07-14 and earlier #360 bounce): sparse/NO_COLOR-looking TTYs are unacceptable on real terminals. Every user-facing surface must look intentionally designed in color mode — not one cyan row and plain chrome.

Surfaces in scope (non-exhaustive, add as found):
- jet ? help palette (interactive + query + F1)
- jet REPL hybrid UI
- jet diagnostics / explain
- jetpack + jetos CLI Theme/Output (nh-class)
- jet env shell prompt receipts/spinners
- tower CLI status/brief human output
- any new interactive TTY app

Law:
- One shared Theme vocabulary (accent, dim, success, warn, error, invert selection, borders) — I8, no per-surface inventing unrelated palettes.
- Color on when TTY && !NO_COLOR (and --color=always|never honored). NO_COLOR keeps a readable monochrome design, not an afterthought.
- Borders, headers, categories, hints, selections, match emphasis all styled in color mode.
- Do not close a frontend/CLI card that ships a new interactive surface without this bar.

First vertical: jet ? Help/Render rich color. Then share Theme into REPL/diagnostics/jetpack.
cards.plan: Use one shared Theme vocabulary and renderer primitives across every TTY surface. Audit help, REPL, diagnostics/explain, jetpack/jetos, env receipts, Tower, and new interactive commands; migrate each without per-surface palettes. TTY auto-color honors NO_COLOR/FORCE_COLOR/--color; monochrome retains hierarchy, focus, contrast, and keyboard behavior. Prove real terminal matrices, redirected bytes, narrow/wide viewports, ANSI safety, accessibility contrast, snapshots, and no semantic output drift.

cards.title: Choose how an output links to callable code
cards.body: Decide the one relationship between a package output and the ordinary Jet function it starts.
cards.plan: Implement D-SHAPE-OUTPUT-CALLABLE1 across parser, sema, TIR lowering, dev/JIT, formatter, package model, CLI selection, semantic index, Canvas, docs, and diagnostics. Runnable typed Outputs hold one checked Jet function reference; sema resolves it before codegen, enforces the Output kind's exact parameter/return/effect/authority contract, rejects ambiguity or mismatch with Jet-owned snapshots, and carries a resolved callable identity into dumb codegen. Preserve ceremony-free standalone `fn run`; inside a Package, D-ECO-OUTPUT-DEFAULT1's deterministic selection is the sole selection path. No string symbol lookup, generated Rust name, runtime reflection, second callable wrapper, or rustc diagnostic. Prove free functions, qualified functions, moved/renamed source, stale locks, each runnable Output kind, formatter/grammar stability, inspect/Canvas reconstruction, and AOT/dev parity.

cards.plan: Implement D-SHAPE-PLACE1=A as one place law across whole values, fields, indexes, and ranges: bare place is a read-only non-copying projection when sema can prove it; `&place` is an exclusive mutable projection; `~place` is an owned copy. Named `View<T>`/`ViewMut<T>` remain exactly where D-MEM-VIEWRET1=B requires public returned/stored provenance contracts, and D-COMPUTE-TYPE1=D retains `View<T>` as the compute projection; their local acquisition follows the same place law. Build on #535's landed copy spelling and #649's unified provenance/alias fact graph. Prove invalidation, resize, overlap/disjointness, nested/maximal places, call results and bounds, method receivers, temporaries, branches, loops, generics, tasks, TIR/AOT/dev parity, diagnostics, docs/examples/grammars/snapshots.

cards.title: Memory audit: distinct allocator runtimes — Arena, Bump, Fixed, slab
cards.body: 2026-07-15 owner audit: Arena, Bump, Pool, and Fixed currently wrap the same vector-of-boxes runtime (crates/jet-codegen/src/Prelude/Mem.rs) and do not provide distinct contiguous-bump, fixed-buffer, or slab behavior. Implement honest distinct runtimes; surface arena retention facts (bulk cleanup may retain more than individual destruction — bounds and high-water facts belong in contracts, see transitive-facts card). No user-syntax change expected; if contract surface needed, that lands in the fact-vocabulary ballot.
cards.plan: Replace the shared vector-of-boxes facade with honest runtimes under the already-ratified public shape. D-ALLOC1/C/D own constructors plus alloc/reset; D-SHAPE-RESOURCE2=A owns terminal `close(^allocator)` and retires free. Arena uses stable bulk-owned storage; Bump is contiguous monotonic allocation; Fixed uses caller-provided bounded storage with deterministic exhaustion; Pool/slab uses size-class/free-list reuse and generation-safe handles where exposed. Prove alignment, drop order, reuse, exhaustion, nested allocation, thread policy, high-water/retention facts, no hidden heap on Fixed, AOT/dev behavior, and semantic benchmarks.

cards.title: Implement common marker scoping and provenance
cards.body: Implement D-MARK-SCOPE1 after ratification. Define one compiler-owned applicability matrix for marker placement at block, function, module, and package levels. Preserve I1: package or module declarations may tighten unsafe policy but never authorize unsafe operations outside a user-written #Unsafe block or function. Keep site-specific value, authority, function-proof, and field-wire markers at their exact legal sites. Effective marker facts must carry source provenance through sema, diagnostics, tooling, AOT, and dev execution.
cards.plan: After #534 completes D-SHAPE2's single `@Rule` marker migration, implement only D-MARK-SCOPE1=A's common scope/applicability/provenance ladder. Package settings enter through the ratified `package.jet` `policy:` field; source rules use the post-migration `@Rule` form at module, function, or block scope. One compiler-owned registry matrix defines each rule's legal echelons, inheritance, same-key override or merge, tightening law, conflicts, and effective-source provenance. Authority, unsafe, taint, sanitizer, and wire rules cannot widen beyond their sound sites. Parser, formatter, sema, semantic index, diagnostics, and `jet explain` consume the same matrix. This card does not implement memory facts, GC promotion, a collector, or GC reports.

cards.title: Test isolation: key_rotation_warns_not_errors flakes on HOME/helper race
cards.body: Full-suite flake (verify-full 2026-07-15, ~intermittent): tests/pkg.rs:3782 key_rotation_warns_not_errors reds with E1246 signature-verification-failed. NOT the base64url canonicality bug (#663) — canonical generated signatures don't explain genuine-signature mismatch. Worker diagnosis (isolated 10x green): process-global HOME race. Tests overwrite a cache-selected crypto helper while mutating HOME at tests/pkg.rs:73, but KEYS_LOCK (tests/pkg.rs:3423) guards only JET_KEYS_DIR; concurrent sign/verify select different real/fake helpers under parallel gate load. Fix: widen the test lock to cover HOME/helper selection, or make helper selection not read process-global HOME. Test-only; signing path fail-closed behavior untouched.
cards.plan: Fix the test race in `tests/pkg.rs` with one existing lock: remove the separate `KEYS_LOCK` and make `with_keys` take `STORE_LOCK`, which already surrounds all three `install_closed_status_crypto_helper` callers while they temporarily change process-global `HOME` and write the HOME-selected cached helper. Audit every `with_keys` and helper-installer call for nesting before the change. Keep `cached_crypto_helper_path`, signing, verification, E1246, and key-rotation product behavior unchanged. Prove the fix by repeatedly running the rotation test alongside the three entropy/helper tests under the normal parallel harness, then targeted pkg tests and full verification; do not hide the race with global single-thread execution.

cards.title: Choose one identifier casing law
cards.body: Owner wants one enforced casing law across the whole language; the surface today is a documented mix (effect keywords Pascal vs lowercase keywords, module split, constant spelling drift, unenforced S54 convention). Ballot D-SHAPE-CASE1 presents PascalCase-everywhere vs snake_case-everywhere vs strict machine-enforced two-tier. Interacts with D-SHAPE3b (Val/None/Ok/Err), D-CASING1 (markers), S54. Outcome drives a migration slice + lint E-code; sequence BEFORE the mass example-touching law cards so snapshots re-bless once.
cards.plan: D-SHAPE-CASE1 is the sole current gate. After ratification, encode the chosen law as one compiler-owned category table and migrate the complete surface without compatibility aliases: A makes every identifier PascalCase; B makes every identifier snake_case and amends conflicting prior casing laws; C enforces PascalCase type-like names and snake_case value-like names. For C, immediately raise the ballot's three named follow-up decisions for effect-keyword, generic-module-template, and constant spelling before touching those ambiguous categories; unambiguous categories proceed from the ratified table. Implement lexer/parser/sema name-category checks, formatter-preserving behavior, one coded diagnostic with precise category/fix, LSP/rename support, docs/examples/snapshots/grammars, package/API migration checks, and AOT/dev-neutral behavior.

questions.text: I need a much more thorough analysis. Give me a bunch more languages showing casing for multiple code excerpts and explain real world tradeoffs extensively, including the implications of prescribing style -> where enterprises may have internal style guides that conflict -> how often does this happen? Is this an issue elsewhere?
questions.answer:
Survey. Nearly every language designed after 2010 prescribes a casing convention. They converge on the same two-tier shape: types are PascalCase, values are snake_case or camelCase. They differ mainly in how the rule is enforced. The ballot's comparisons section now carries 15 languages with code; summary below.

Enforcement varies by level. Grammar-enforced languages make casing part of parsing, so violation is a syntax error: Haskell, Elm, Erlang, Prolog, and partly Ruby. Rust warns through default compiler lints. Dart, Kotlin, and Go enforce through shipped tools. Python, Java, C#, Swift, and TypeScript rely on convention and optional linters. C++ sets no shared default at all.

Enterprise style-guide conflicts. These happen almost only in languages that never enforced a law from the start. Where casing is grammar-enforced, conflict is impossible and nobody forks: no Haskell, Elm, or Erlang shop runs a lowercase-type house style. Go overloads casing with visibility, and it is universally accepted; Google's and Uber's guides build on it rather than against it.

Rust shops keep the non_snake_case warnings; the #[allow] escape exists mainly for FFI, not house style. The conflicts cluster where no law shipped. Python's PEP 8 is unenforced, so legacy camelCase survives for decades in unittest, logging, and Twisted. C++ and JavaScript set no default, so Google, LLVM, Qt, and Unreal each wrote a different guide, and reading across codebases suffers.

The empirical pattern is consistent. A language born with an enforced law sees internal guides adopt it, not fight it. A language that shipped without one grows many competing house styles that never reconcile.

Implications of prescribing style. A single enforced law speeds onboarding and reading, because a reader infers a name's category from its shape without opening its definition. It also makes tooling predictable: derives, LSP rename, and doc generation can rely on category-from-name. Codegen output stays stable because names map one way.

One cost is real. Foreign names must keep their original casing, so any prescribed law needs a narrow, sanctioned escape for interop. Rust uses #[allow(non_snake_case)] on extern items; Dart suppresses the lint on FFI and JS interop. Jet will need the same narrow escape for FFI bindings. That belongs in a follow-up decision, not invented here.

Where this shows up elsewhere. Formatters are the precedent. gofmt, black, and prettier proved that teams accept a prescribed style when it is universal and tool-enforced from day one. The resentment cases are retrofits, where a rule arrives after a large codebase already chose differently. Enforcing casing from the start avoids that retrofit.

On this evidence C is the right law. It is the only option that keeps the type-versus-value signal every post-2010 language preserves, while still being machine-enforced so no file can drift.

questions.text: I don’t understand what this means, dumb it down to plain language
questions.answer:
Plain version. Today your build script can look at one type at a time (to derive things). This ballot asks: may the build script also READ the finished, fully-checked program — every package, type, and function — and report its own errors?

Concrete use: your team rule is "every public function that touches the network must take a timeout". Today that rule lives on a wiki or an external linter that half-parses Jet and drifts. With B, your build entry can loop over all functions and emit a real Jet diagnostic — same format as compiler errors, and the API forces you to fill in code + what/why/fix, so quality stays I4-grade.

Hard limits that keep it safe: READ ONLY (build code cannot change your program, ever — that is rung C, still frozen); runs only from YOUR chosen build entry, never when merely importing a library (a dependency cannot run rules or code inside your build); and if you don't write one, nothing changes.

B = "the compiler will show your program to your build script and let it complain, nothing more."

cards.title: Polyglot Phase 1: systems floor — inline tier, inline asm, C++ binder
cards.body: From docs/proposals/polyglot.md. Adds the missing fourth D-FFI-UNIFY1 tier (#Foreign(<lang>) inline bodies with the Jet signature as checked contract), the assembly floor (#Foreign(asm) inside #Unsafe, typed operands), and the cpp.* binder (clang bindgen, opaque class handles, exceptions -> T ? CppError, on-demand template instantiation). One ballot per decision: D-FFI-INLINE1, D-FFI-ASM1, D-FFI-CPP1. Gates every later phase: inline tier shape is reused by all languages.
cards.plan: Implement the ratified systems floor on D-FFI-UNIFY1's checked boundary. Inline #Foreign bodies keep Jet signatures authoritative and re-enter validation; raw foreign bodies follow D-FFI-RAWBODY1. #Foreign(asm) remains inside #Unsafe with D-FFI-ASMOPS1=C typed operand contracts and target/clobber audit. cpp.* bindgen uses opaque ownership, explicit templates, exception -> T ? CppError, callbacks, cache/provenance, and real compiler/link proof. No unchecked source injection or compiler dependency leak.

Share transport helpers; do not create six semantic FFI systems.

cards.title: Parser correctness policy: contracts, adversarial corpus, and dependency gates
cards.body: Audit every hand-rolled protocol/config parser: LSP JSON, manifest TOML subset, SemVer/ranges, C prototypes, and registry/advisory formats. For each, publish its accepted grammar, reject unsupported cases deliberately, add hostile-input coverage, and fix correctness holes. Jet owns every diagnostic. If a protocol cannot be made correct within I6, stop that slice and raise a separate dependency-exception ballot before adding any crate.
cards.plan: Inventory parser entrypoints and current documented promises. Build a parser-by-parser contract table. Add adversarial tests for escapes, Unicode, nesting, malformed input, recovery, overflow, and ambiguous versions/prototypes. Tighten contracts or implementations until behavior and docs agree. Any external parser remains owner-gated under I6.

cards.title: Plan affine quantity point semantics
cards.body: Prepare point, difference, declaration, conversion, and diagnostic ballot only after dimensional algebra ownership is ratified.
cards.plan: All quantity choices are ratified. Implement D-SHAPE-QUANTITY1=A compiler-owned zero-cost dimensions, D-QUANTITY-DECL1=A exact scale/offset declarations, D-QUANTITY-TYPE1=A generic Dimension/Kind bounds, D-QUANTITY-POINT1=A Point/Delta algebra, and D-QUANTITY-CONVERT1=B exact same-dimension implicit conversion in mixed arithmetic, arguments, and bindings. The finer operand unit wins mixed arithmetic; equal scales keep the left unit. Point conversion applies scale plus offset and Delta conversion applies scale only. Sema never rounds silently: inexact or overflowing boundaries reject with the destination-owned from_* or from_*_rounded fix. package.jet explicit_units and narrower #Policy(explicit_units) require written conversions through the normal policy ladder. Finish declaration, sema, API/Codable/semver, diagnostics, inspect, examples, grammar, and AOT/dev parity without a second conversion path.

questions.text: Remember one of the goals is not to baby experts. There can be value in having explicit conversions but in practice I would expect people doing pragmatic work to want implicit conversions which would be defined in advance anyway by the unit family. Maybe have some kind of marker/policy that can disable implicit conversions? For example, in my case if I was doing cad measurements, I would probably name something like inner_diameter_mm and length_m. It would be annoying to have to do mathematical operations with tons of dot methods just to manually convert everything. Implicit should be default with an explicit opt in
questions.answer: Agreed, and the ballot now recommends exactly that. Reworked option B: same-dimension units convert on their own wherever the family ratio makes the conversion exact — mixed arithmetic (lands on the finer unit so whole numbers stay exact), argument passing, and binding all just work, so length + inner_diameter is one plus sign, no dot-method chain. The guardrail kept: the compiler never rounds silently — a non-exact conversion (1500m into whole km) is a compile error naming the from_meter_rounded fix, so implicit never loses precision. The opt-in you asked for rides the policy ladder you just ratified: policy: .{ explicit_units: true } in package.jet, or #Policy(explicit_units) at module/function/block, restores explicit-only in that scope. Ballot updated and ready to ratify (rec B).

cards.title: Subjectless multi-arm if for ordered condition dispatch
cards.body: Reduce repeated `else if` chains with a subjectless `if { condition -> body }` form. Preserve `if` as Jet's only branching keyword and reuse existing arm bodies, first-match ordering, pattern-test bindings, fallback rules, formatter shape, and checked TIR lowering. This card is gated on D-IFGUARD1; no syntax or implementation lands before owner ratification.
cards.plan: After D-IFGUARD1 is ratified, implement only the selected surface. For a subjectless form, parse `if {` as ordered Boolean arms and reuse the existing dispatch pipeline through a compiler-private Bool subject; this is lowering only, not a source-level comparison. Do not add another keyword, AST mechanism, or codegen path. Sema checks every head as Bool. A pattern binding reaches the body only from a leading pattern test joined through `&&`; bindings under `||` never enter body scope. Evaluate heads once from top to bottom, run only the first matching body, and apply the ratified fallback law. Update Syntax.rs decision adjacency, parser and formatter, sema, diagnostics and UI snapshots, grammar/editor support, examples and goldens, formal/spec prose, Canvas projection/editing, and dev/AOT parity. Phase 1 (computed alias) + Phase 7 (web/DOM backend) verified 100% already-shipped, not stubs — confirmed via targeted tests: web_build (13/13), web_dev (3/3), corelib core_module_items_covers_known_core_modules, tir reactive_scope_marker, plus a manual native+web dual-run of examples/features/web/ui_web_reactive.jet through real node, byte-identical output. D-HTMLPAIR1 amended: added option B (manifest target field, composed with #Html file marker + precedence chain). D-OSTARGET1/D-WEBDEFAULT1 reviewed under the magic/expert/audit lens: sound as written, no change.

devserver ergonomics (owner feedback): (1) devserver.app() — new zero-arg constructor meaning watch the file jet dev launched; run_dev_entry passes the canonical absolute path to the compiled dev() program via JET_DEV_FILE, so no path literal is needed at all and it works from any invocation directory (kills the prior repo-root-only caveat). Clear error if the binary is run outside jet dev. (2) for_app(path) now canonicalizes relative-or-absolute against invocation cwd up front. (3) .html(path) already resolved against the app files dir (matches #Html semantics); absolute paths pass through via Path::join. (4) Real bug found during foreign-cwd verification: DevServer shelled out to bare jet from PATH — wrong version risk generally, and the nix devshells cwd-sensitive jet wrapper broke outright under the staging cwd (initial build failed; earlier 200s that looked like success were actually the owners own stale 197 server on 8080 — process-tree check caught it). Fix: run_dev_entry passes its own current_exe() as JET_BIN; DevServer prefers JET_BIN over PATH. 196s dev() is now just devserver.app() + serve(). New test jet_dev_app_zero_arg_watches_launched_file (no PATH doctoring — proves JET_BIN/JET_DEV_FILE plumbing alone suffices). Verified end-to-end from a foreign cwd incl. rebuild-on-save. Full workspace + golden green.

Big pivot per owner: dev-server config moves from CLI flags/file-top markers into real Jet code. Built fn dev() as a well-known optional entry point (like main, no new syntax): jet dev <file> checks for it first; if present, compiles the file NATIVELY with dev() swapped in as the real entry (AST-level rename before codegen, reusing the same you-can-swap-entry idea as jet test/jet bench, not a new CompileMode), runs the resulting binary, and dev()s own Jet code configures+starts a real core.devserver value (devserver.for_app(file).html(...).port(...).serve()). The running compiled program cant link the compiler, so serve() shells out to jet build --target=web for every rebuild (subprocess, not a library call) -- new Prelude/DevServer.rs, std-only. If no fn dev() exists, falls straight through to todays default (jet dev --target=web / #Target(Web) inference), unchanged -- verified via the pre-existing test suite untouched.

Found + fixed a real ordering bug during my own verification (not caught by the automated test, which used a fixture without #Target(Web)): the #Target(Web)-inferred built-in server check ran BEFORE the fn dev() check, so any file with both markers -- e.g. 196, which already had #Target(Web) from earlier this session -- could never actually reach the new path; it silently fell back to the old built-in server every time, looking identical from the outside (same port, same content served). Reordered so fn dev() is checked first (more specific override wins). Verified for real this time by checking the process tree for the actual compiled child binary + confirming a live jet build subprocess-driven rebuild-on-save, not just that a server responded on the port.

fn build() (comptime/build procedure) intentionally NOT built -- overlaps unratified card #38, owner asked to scope separately.

Re-blessed one stale ui/ snapshot (core.devserver in E1001s known-module-list fix text). Full cargo test --workspace + golden green.

1) Clone report: no actual bug. All *.clone() reaching JS were already fixed; the confusion was L0801 (a pre-existing lint) warning 3x per build on 197 for capturing Signal/Backend handles into reactive_render closures -- the idiomatic pattern every example this session uses. Flagged as possibly miscalibrated (cheap Rc-clone captures shouldnt need take()) but not changed without owner confirmation.

2) D-HTMLPAIR1 raised+built: #Html("path.html") file-level marker (same family as #Target(Web)), explicit instead of the silent <stem>.html convention; missing file is now a loud build error, not a silent fallback. New Program/LoadedModule.html_path AST field, WebArtifacts.explicit_html_path, precedence explicit-marker > sibling-convention > generic page.

3) #Js reorg attempt on 197: tried grouping via existing #Target(Js) module {} (cascades bucket to members, confirmed). Found 2 real bugs this exposed: struct declared inside inline module invisible to sibling fns (general E0119, no web involved), and moving a fn into a module changes native codegen enough to break struct-field-forward cloning (I2 rustc rejection). Both documented in 197s source, NOT fixed (routed around) -- reverted to the working per-fn #Js tags. Module-grouping is NOT safe to recommend yet.

4) Real regression caught+fixed during dogfooding: first cut of D-WEBDEFAULT1 inferred web for jet run too, which tried to exec a .wasm/.js bundle as a native binary and failed. jet run now never infers from marker/manifest (native-only, requires explicit --target=web); build/dev/check still infer. New regression test jet_cli_run_never_infers_web_target_from_marker.

196 and 197 now both carry explicit #Target(Web) + #Html(...) (dogfooded). 4 new tests total this round. Full cargo test --workspace + golden green.

Flagship showcase (197_ui_showcase.jet/.html): all 5 mechanisms wired together for real -- typed View tree (native-only cluster, printed), typed Color->hex (real integer-arithmetic conversion feeding ui.node_color, not a shortcut), component-kit-style composed functions (stat_card/paint_stat_card), Clock-driven tween motion (Fuel card, real requestAnimationFrame loop), two independent reactive.signal-driven cards (Boosts counter, Fuel elapsed-time), all painting real DOM elements. Found+fixed 3 more real JS-codegen gaps (StructLit construction, to_float/to_int, sema-inserted .clone() -- all were silently producing undefined, a real correctness hazard) plus a multi-node DOM-identity collision (scope-keyed element registry, was single global querySelector). New test web_showcase_dashboard_roundtrip.

Also shipped: --port=<N> flag on jet dev --target=web (explicit port fails loud, no silent fallback). And D-WEBDEFAULT1 (raised open in Tower, owner gave clear direction live in chat but formal ratification still pending): #Target(Web) file-level marker + pkg.jet target:"web" field, so jet run/dev/build infer the web backend without --target=web every time; CLI flag still overrides both. New Program.default_target AST field, PackageMeta.target manifest field, effective_target()/manifest_default_target() helpers in main.rs. 2 new integration tests + 1 new ui/ snapshot (E0003 on #Target(Web) module, invalid position). Full cargo test --workspace + golden green.

Phase 7 extension continued (owner feedback): (1) visual polish on 196_ui_web_click.html (dark-mode card layout, gradient background, real button styling) and the generic auto-emitted index.html (both now genuinely presentable, not bare unstyled boxes). (2) Real jet dev <file> --target=web command (Source/CmdDevWeb.rs, new): std-only (I6) TCP static file server + mtime-poll rebuild-on-save (reuses file_mtime from run_dev) + browser live-reload via polled /__jet_dev_version + location.reload(), so viewing/iterating on a Jet web app needs zero Node/npm. New test tests/web_dev.rs (spawns the real jet binary, confirms serve + real rebuild-on-edit, 5/5 stable runs). Found + fixed a real intermittent rename-race in the staging-swap (fs::rename occasionally saw a not-yet-visible file under concurrent load) with a bounded retry — reproducible only under heavy concurrent nix develop load in this sandbox, not clearly a real-machine issue, but the retry is cheap and correct either way. tools/web-serve.mjs (the earlier Node workaround) is now superseded — kept for now, not deleted, since it still works standalone. Full cargo test --workspace + golden green after a stray /tmp nix-shell buildup was cleared (unrelated env issue, not a regression).

Raised D-OSTARGET1 (3 options: extend #Target with Os.* variants / new dedicated #Os marker / manifest-level gating in pkg.jet, rec=A) rather than inventing syntax. Separately, this sandbox has no GTK/AppKit/Win32 dev headers or pkg-config available (verified) — even once D-OSTARGET1 is ratified, a real linked native backend cannot be built/tested here without a flake/devShell change to add platform toolkit dependencies, which is its own decision the owner should see before its assumed. Card stays in deciding for Phase 8 only; do not close c134 until D-OSTARGET1 is ratified and a native backend actually builds+runs behind it.

Phase 7 done: web/DOM backend. Codegen/Web.rs gained lambda emission + reactive.signal -> jetDom.makeSignal + ui.reactive_render dispatch; DomRuntime.js gained a dependency-tracked reactive shim mirroring Rust JetSignal (still in-memory command log, no real document API — no browser under node, by design). New web_reactive_dom_snapshot_roundtrip test in tests/web_build.rs actually runs the emitted JS via node and diffs stdout against a fixture (the web DOM snapshot). Example 195_ui_web_reactive.jet runs identically native + web (both expected outputs verified). JS codegen scope intentionally narrow (documented list of supported constructs). Verified myself: cargo build clean, web_build 6/6 green, native jet run correct output. Flagged not fixed: D-JSBIND1 referenced as ratified in code comments but has no standalone row in syntax-decisions.md.

Phase 6 done: a11y. JetAriaRole (Button/TextInput/Label/Container) + JetUiNode.role + keyboard focus routing (Tab cycles a focus-group list) in Prelude/Ui.rs; new ui.node_role/aria_role_* constructors (existing ui.node untouched, no golden regressions). E2930 (empty accessible label on interactive node) + E2931 (duplicate label across focus-group) as Severity::Lint diagnostics, filtered out of build/run/check/emit output and only surfaced via new jet lint --a11y <file> CLI subcommand (Source/CLI.rs, main.rs, CmdDevTools.rs) — verified jet run/build on the same problem files succeed with zero a11y output (D-A11YGATE1=B non-blocking requirement held). Both checks are static/literal-only by design (documented scope, not a heuristic). Example 194_ui_a11y.jet + 2 tests/ui_lint snapshots, all verified by hand + targeted test runs (golden, cli, lint_snapshots, ui_backend, decisions, ui, jet-sema --lib all green).

Phase 5 done: motion. Plain user-space tween() (smoothstep ease, clamped) over the already-real injectable Clock (core.time.clock) + reactive.signal/derived — motion value is a pure Computed<T> of elapsed clock time, never imperatively .set(). No new compiler machinery, no new bugs hit. Example 193_ui_motion.jet, golden-tested with exact binary-fraction outputs (byte-exact, no float flakiness).

Phase 4 done: ownable component kit. jetpack add <Name> (Button/Label/Input/Container, exact-case catalog match) copies embedded .jet source into components/ in the user project (Jetpack/Components.rs, include_str!-embedded from Jetpack/components/*.jet); refuses to clobber an already-owned file. Existing jetpack add <source>:<pkg> package-ref path unaffected (verified). Example 192_ui_component_kit.jet composes all four over one View tree, golden-tested. 3 unit tests + full e2e binary run verified. Found + documented 2 more real compiler bugs (not fixed, routed around): (1) I2 ICE — forwarding an unmodified fn param into an enum dot-variant field moves out of a shared ref instead of cloning (E0507); (2) sema gap — list-literal element position does not get dot-variant type inference that struct-field position gets, and E0330s own suggested EnumName.Variant.{} fallback does not parse either.

Phase 3 done: typed Style (flat record per D-STYLESHAPE1) + Color + Length/LengthUnit as plain user-space Jet struct/enum (same recipe as Phase 2 View, zero new core-type registration). No backend wiring into JetPaintCmd since color:String there is not yet settable from Jet source (nothing load-bearing to wire into). No new diagnostics — construction errors already covered by generic E0303. Found + documented (not fixed, out of scope) a real TIR-subset-coverage bug: a struct field of a distinct/#UnitFamily type ICEs codegen (worked around using flat struct+enum Length instead of #UnitFamily sugar). Example examples/features/191_ui_typed_style.jet, golden-tested.

Phase 1 done: computed alias fix + 3 pre-existing test-compile breaks fixed (Reflect.rs Span import, TIR/mod.rs ProgramBundle missing fields, 2 stale-syntax unit tests, jet-driver fixture path) — cargo test --workspace now fully green (was broken on master before this card). Phase 2 done: named-payload enum variants (S30, VariantPayload::Named) now construct via .Variant.{ field: val } / Type.Variant.{ field: val } per D-UITREE1s ratified spelling — this was previously UNIMPLEMENTED (EnumLitArg::Named was dead code in the parser despite full sema/codegen/formatter support). Added parser production (enum_lit_named_fields), fixed a codegen pattern-match bug (positional variant patterns fabricated f0/f1 instead of real field names for Named payloads), fixed a P0 sema infinite-recursion bug (is_cloneable had no cycle guard, so ANY self-referential type crashed the compiler with a stack overflow the moment it flowed through a reactive.derived/effect/computed closure capture check). View tree + diff-based rerender demonstrated in examples/features/190_ui_view_tree.jet (golden-tested), fmt round-trip test added, ui snapshot added for the new E0303 fix-text. Full cargo test --workspace green. Remaining: Phase 3 typed styles, Phase 4 component kit, Phase 5 motion, Phase 6 a11y, Phase 7 web backend completion, Phase 8 native backend.

cards.title: corelib audit: core.text — Unicode completeness (case folding, segmentation, width)
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Swift String honesty + ICU floor. Cards #66 (graphemes, normalization) and the unicode slice of #117 are done — verify shipped surface first.

Audit list: NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD normalization (verify); full Unicode case mapping and case folding for upper/lower/caseless-compare (not ASCII-only); grapheme iteration (verify) plus word and sentence segmentation (UAX #29); display width (east-asian width) for terminal alignment; char classification (alphabetic, numeric, whitespace per Unicode); efficient String builder for heavy concatenation; general str utility audit vs Rust str + Python str (splitn/rsplit, trim variants, pad/center, starts/ends combinators, char_indices equivalents). Collation/locale sort: record policy (probably an i18n non-goal for now — state it).

Done means: audit table in docs, gaps shipped with examples + golden tests or recorded as declined non-goals. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan: Finish D-TEXTUNICODE1=A with core.text as the single Unicode algorithm home and String-aware tooling inserting those calls. Verify/complete NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD, full case mapping/folding, grapheme/word/sentence segmentation, D-TEXTWIDTH1=B display width, classification, scalar/UTF-8 helpers, and efficient builder/util parity. Pin Unicode data/version and deterministic behavior; state collation/locale policy explicitly. Prove hostile ill-formed boundaries, large text, AOT/dev parity, docs/examples, and Core rubric status.

Break-test corpora committed under tests/data/unicode/ but conformance tests NOT wired yet. cards.title: corelib audit: core.crypto — misuse-resistant suite (AEAD, signatures, KDF, password hashing)
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: libsodium/age misuse-resistance — high-level envelopes a beginner cannot hold wrong, primitives behind them for experts. Card #64 (crypto push) is done — but the prelude currently exposes only sha256, hmac, and random_bytes; verify what actually shipped (FFI bridge included), then close the gaps.

Scope: authenticated encryption seal/open envelope with one canonical cipher (XChaCha20-Poly1305 or AES-GCM — owner ballot), nonce handling internal (never user-supplied by default); Ed25519 sign/verify; X25519 key exchange; Argon2id password hash + verify with safe defaults; HKDF; SHA-512 and BLAKE3; constant-time comparison; key/secret types that refuse Display (no keys in logs — safe by default); simple key encoding (raw/hex/PEM as needed); file-encryption envelope (age-class). PQ hybrid agility already tracked (#71).

I6: implementations in-house or behind the FFI bridge crate — each new bridge dep is an owner ballot. Done means: each primitive ships with test vectors from the reference specs (RFC/NIST/libsodium vectors) as golden tests.
