cards.title: E3 formal compiler-extension plugin API (D-DX5-B)
cards.body: Implement the owner-ratified optional formal plugin API for tools needing compiler integration, while keeping PATH-discovered jet-* helpers and application target: plugin distinct. First settle the v1 compiler boundary: initial hook stage plus isolation/authority model. Front end retains semantics and diagnostics; plugins cannot make rustc user-visible or mutate unchecked compiler state.
cards.plan: Implement D-DX5-HOOK1=A as one versioned typed read-only post-sema snapshot in an isolated WebAssembly component. Reuse the actual WASM component host owned by jet-pkg-model; do not invent a native in-process loader or reuse application-plugin semantics. Define capability negotiation, deterministic snapshot/schema, symbol/type/effect/span/provenance reads, validated finding/edit responses, limits/timeouts, trust/version policy, and Jet-owned failures. Prove one custom lint plus malformed, incompatible, looping, crashing, and nondeterministic components; preserve PATH jet-* helpers, application target: plugin, I2/I3, and AOT/dev facts.

cards.title: Sigil sweep: # for attributes/instructions/properties, @ for locations/addresses/sources
cards.body: Owner decree 2026-07-23: revert the rule/marker plane from @ back to #. Conceptual split: # marks attributes, instructions, properties; @ marks locations, addresses, sources. Reverses D-SHAPE2/D-MARKERMOVE1's @ plane; restores D-ATTR1's # plane. Highest priority: lands before any parallel in-flight syntax work to avoid rework.
cards.plan:
SCOPE (all gates ratified: D-VERDICT-732-1, D-ATTR4=A, D-LOOPLABEL3=A)
- Flip @ -> # for the whole applied-rule plane: RULE_PREFIX in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax/markers.rs plus every APPLIED_RULES spelling (@Unsafe, @Test, @Pure, @Cli, @Task, @Every, @Target, @Pre/@Post/@Persist, @Inline/@InlineAlways, bundles, serde markers, @DebugOnly, @Meta, @[allow(...)], @[a,b] lists, pub-file/no-prelude/static/inline/SIMD-reduce rules).
- effects_surface.rs already holds ATTR_PREFIX="#" and FOREIGN_AT_ATTR="@" from D-ATTR1; those become authoritative again. Teaching-error direction reverses: @Marker in rule position -> 'attributes use #'.
- D-ATTR4=A: interpolation debug spec flips to {value#Debug}.
- D-LOOPLABEL3=A: loop labels leave @ entirely. New: outer :: loop naming (compile-time label kind in the ordinary namespace), outer.break()/outer.next() dot exits, bare break/next keywords keep working for the innermost loop. outer@ suffix + break outer@ retire with a teaching error; E0988 matrix updated; outer := loop rejected; label-in-value-position is a teaching error. expr ?? outer.break() composes per D-ORRETURN-CANON1.
- STAYS @ pending #733/D-JPK-REF1: provider@target source refs (U6), path@host OS selector (D-JPK-OSHOST1=C). Do NOT touch ref grammar in this card.
- STAYS #: [T#N] fixed-size separator (S76), #Caller(), textkit#1.2.0 version pins (VERSION-#).

FOOTPRINT (measured 2026-07-23): ~182 files with @-marker spellings across examples/docs/crates; docs/spec/diagnostics.md ~104 hits, syntax-decisions.md ~84, spec.md ~54, examples/canon.jet 18; examples/features/basics/labeled_loops.jet for D-LOOPLABEL3.

SLICES (each verified with targeted tests; full suite once at closeout)
1. Syntax registry: flip RULE_PREFIX to #, reconcile effects_surface constants, register :: loop-label form, update decision-ID comments.
2. Lexer/parser: # dispatch in rule position (decl/expr/scope); outer :: loop + dot-exit parsing; wrong-plane fall-throughs (#Wasm/#Js/#Suppress/#Uninit/#Ref retirements) keep behavior under the new prefix.
3. Teaching errors: @Marker -> use-# error; outer@/break outer@ -> use ::/dot-exit error; label-as-value error; each with UI snapshot (I4).
4. Formatter: emit # and :: labels; fmt STABILITY round-trip tests (idempotence alone misses dropped tokens).
5. Sema/LSP/highlights + editors/tree-sitter grammar (zed grammar-repo is generated, do not commit).
6. Sweep examples/**.jet + golden outputs (I5), canon.jet + labeled_loops.jet first; rm -rf ~/.cache/jet/build before smoke.
7. Docs sweep: syntax-decisions.md, spec.md, diagnostics.md, philosophy refs; UI snapshots re-blessed.
8. Closeout: fresh-binary smoke, one full-suite run, Sol review.

COORDINATION
- No other card may introduce @-plane or outer@-label spellings until this lands; in-flight branches rebase on the flip commit.
- Land slices 1-4 as one atomic sweep so no split-brain surface ships.
- Ref grammar (#733, D-JPK-REF1) is owner-gated and explicitly out of scope here.

cards.title: Silent no-op: list element field writes are dropped
cards.body:
Ship-blocker from the 2026-07-23 persona audit (Klaus, systems dev).

Repro (/tmp/persona-klaus/mut.jet): `ps[0].x = 11` and `ps[0].x += 1` compile clean, mutate a temporary, and the old values print. Plain `ns[1] += 5` IS rejected with a teaching error — so the accepted spelling is the broken one.

This kills array-of-structs code (games, sims) with silent wrong physics. It breaks the spirit of I3: sema passes what codegen drops. Fix first, before any polish work.

log.text: Review finding — crates/jet-sema/src/Sema/CheckerCore/statements.rs:41 and crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/emit/statements.rs:822: indexed compound field assignment does not preserve Jet operator-hook semantics. Sema accepts hs[0].value += rhs when value implements Jet Add because compound_field_type cannot resolve Expr::Index; the new emitter then writes native Rust +=. Jet generates user_Add, not std::ops::AddAssign, so rustc rejects a sema-approved program, violating criterion 1 and I2. Repro check with a [Holder] whose Vec2 field implements Add reports no Jet problems. Fix by resolving and rewriting the indexed field hook through the existing Add method spine, or emit E0362 before TIR; add a regression for this indexed user-operator case. Numeric Int = and += paths pass targeted TIR, golden, strict interpreter/JIT/AOT three-way, fresh build/smoke, Pool parity, and columnar runtime/UI checks. Broad jit_coverage_audit still has known unrelated manifest drift; the new collections/struct_list_mutation entry is observed covered and IndexFieldAssign reports 2 covered, 0 gaps.
Master integration agent: do not stage, commit, or merge sidequests-implementation while these cards are active. Wait for explicit closeout handoff; sidequest workers own this worktree.

Investigation: parser and sema accept a mutable list-element field place, but TIR lowers the index through clone-returning jet_index_vec. AOT and default dev print old values. Forced interpreter gives E2201. Planned fix: use a bounds-checked mutable list place in shared TIR lowering; keep the interpreter teaching boundary.

cards.title: Diagnostics polish batch from the 2026-07-23 persona audit
cards.body:
Ten cheap diagnostic fixes found by the persona audit. Each is a wording, dedupe, or teaching gap — no new syntax, no owner decision.

1. `continue` gives E0003 (value not used) and never says Jet spells it `next`. Add a teaching error. Worst beginner trap found.
2. `?? { block }` is invalid and the fix text shows no working alternative.
3. The same E0107 appears twice for one span — dedupe.
4. A positional multi-payload variant `Hit(String, Int)` fails with a raw "expected `)`". Teach the S30 rule: one payload positional, two or more use named fields.
5. E0119 says "use `random.Rng` here" while E0112 rejects naming `random.Rng`; bare `Rng` works. Resolve the clash.
6. The `_` discard binding cascades into nonsense errors ("give away a copy instead (`~_`)").
7. `@Unsafe` with no reason gets lint L3101, and the same run prints "ok: no problems". The two statements clash.
8. L0504 flags `total := 0.0` as money. False positive.
9. E1004 leaks internal jargon ("documented M10 items").
10. `&particles[idx]` fix text teaches a copy that cannot change the list. Name the `&xs[a..b]` write-window idiom instead.

cards.title: Semantic-core TIR: structured facts, no Rust text inside the IR
cards.body:
Owner directive 2026-07-24: one compiler core; every engine is a lens on it; a feature is written once and works in jet run and jet build the same day.

Why this card exists: TIR is the shared program form, but it carries pre-rendered Rust text (ty_clause strings, Rust place strings like (*user_x), field_rust names, literal text such as vec![1i64, 2i64]). Only the AOT Rust emitter can consume that text. The Cranelift JIT needs structured data, so every feature needs a second hand-written JIT lowering, and 262 example programs sit in tests/jit_gaps.txt today. This card removes the Rust text from TIR so one lowering serves every engine.

This is the root card of the one-core rework. Cards for the canonical interpreter, tiered jet run, and the desugaring wave build on it. Decision D-ONECORE1 on this card picks the overall structure.
cards.plan:
1. Inventory every TIR field that holds rendered Rust text (kw, ty_clause, place, field_rust, tmp names, literal strings). Post the checked list to this card's log.
2. Replace them variant by variant with structured facts: typed places, typed literals, type references, symbol ids. Move all Rust text rendering into the emit layer of jet-codegen.
3. Hold byte parity while doing it: golden/snapshot suites and tests/dev.rs::dev_default_matches_compiled_binary stay green after each variant lands.
4. Update the Cranelift lowering to read only structured facts; delete every string-parsing workaround in crates/jet-jit/src/jit/lower_ctx.rs.
5. Write the core TIR contract into docs/spec/architecture.md (R12 restated per D-ONECORE1) and hand the frozen-contract work to e9 card #668.

Acceptance: no field of TStmt/TExpr holds Rust source text; the JIT lowering contains no Rust-string parsing; full example corpus and parity gates green.
Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/**, crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/** (emit layer), crates/jet-jit/src/jit/** (reads only), docs/spec/architecture.md (R12 section), touched tests.

cards.title: Tiered jet run: Cranelift per function, interpreter deopt, retire E2211
cards.body:
Today a Cranelift coverage gap in jet run is a hard stop: error E2211 tells the user to go run jet build instead (D-LENS-RUN1, card #728). 262 example programs hit that wall. Once the canonical interpreter (#777) defines runtime behavior, a gap no longer needs to be a wall: the JIT can compile the functions it covers and hand the rest to the interpreter, the way the JVM and V8 tier their execution.

This card makes jet run tiered: tier 1 is native Cranelift, tier 0 is the interpreter, chosen per function, same observable behavior either way. E2211 retires as a user-facing error. tests/jit_gaps.txt stays, but as a performance ratchet, not a feature gate.

Decision D-LENS-RUN2 on this card picks what the user sees at a deopt. It amends ratified D-LENS-RUN1, which forbade any fallback while the only fallback was a different engine with different coverage. The interpreter changes that premise: the fallback IS the reference engine.
cards.plan:
1. Add per-function tier selection to the JIT backend: lower each function through Cranelift; on a named unsupported reason, bind that function to the interpreter instead of failing the program.
2. Make cross-tier calls work both directions (native calling interpreted and back) over the existing host-shim boundary in crates/jet-jit.
3. Retire E2211 per the D-LENS-RUN2 outcome; keep the named gap reasons as internal traces. Add the expert visibility surface the outcome names (for example jet run --trace-tiers).
4. Convert tests/jit_gaps.txt into a performance ratchet: gaps may only shrink; a new gap needs a named reason in the same diff; CI fails on silent growth.
5. Extend the #727/#730 differential gate: every corpus program must produce identical stdout, stderr, and exit code under pure-interpreter, mixed-tier, and AOT runs.

Acceptance: no runnable checked program fails jet run for coverage reasons; the differential gate is green across tier mixes; hot-swap and resident dev still work.
Owned paths: crates/jet-jit/**, Source/Interpreter.rs, Source/CmdCompile.rs (run routing), tests/jit_gaps.txt, tests/dev.rs, docs/spec/diagnostics.md (E2211 retirement).

cards.title: Core-shrink wave: surface features desugar in lowering, engines stay untouched
cards.body:
The reason backends fall behind is that TIR is wide: it carries one construct per surface feature (for-in forms, map literals, string interpolation, destructuring, fan-out), and every engine must handle every construct. This card narrows TIR to a small core by desugaring surface features into existing core constructs during lowering, after #776 gives the core clean structured form.

End state: adding a surface feature is a parser + sema + lowering change only. The interpreter, the Cranelift tier, and the Rust emitter see constructs they already support, so both jet run and jet build work the day the lowering lands. That is the structural guarantee behind the owner's one-core directive.
cards.plan:
1. Rank TIR constructs by backend cost: for each executable variant, count the emit arm, the Cranelift arm, and the interpreter arm it forces. Post the ranking to the card log.
2. Desugar the expensive wide constructs into core ones at lowering, one per slice: for-in over literals and collections, map/set literals, string interpolation, tuple/struct/list destructuring, fan-out.
3. Each slice deletes the matching special-case arm from every engine in the same diff. Parity gates stay green per slice.
4. Prove the guarantee on a real feature: implement one small ratified surface feature end to end and show the diff touches no engine files.
5. Record the final core construct list in the TIR contract doc for the e9 freeze card (#668).

Acceptance: measured drop in per-engine match arms; one demonstration feature ships with zero engine-file changes; no new entries in tests/jit_gaps.txt during the wave.
Owned paths: crates/jet-codegen/src/Codegen/TIR/** (lowering), matching arm deletions in crates/jet-jit/** and the emit layer and the evaluator, touched tests.

cards.title: Universal typed-literal head: Type.{ body } for every type
cards.body: Generalize S29/D-DOTCTOR1/2: any type may head a .{ } literal body — scalars U8.{250}, lists [U8].{42,0,0}, maps [String: Int].{}, fixed arrays [U8#3].{255,128,0}, and one-expression assertion bodies Int.{ fetch_rows() }. Body elaborates against the head exactly like an expected-type position; it never converts. Amends D-EMPTY: [T].{} is the explicit empty; bare [] stays contextual.
cards.plan:
blockedBy: none

Authority: D-DOTCTOR3=A (ratified). Amends S29 / D-DOTCTOR1 / D-DOTCTOR2 and D-EMPTY.

Goal: Any type may head a .{ } literal body. The body elaborates against the head like an expected-type position. It never converts.

## 1. Syntax authority
- Add the D-DOTCTOR3 entry in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs.
- Append the syntax-decisions.md log: universal Type.{ body }; [T].{} is the explicit empty; bare [] stays contextual; Int.{ expr } is a one-expression assertion.
- Run jet devtools grammars and bless grammar outputs.

## 2. Parser
Owned: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Expressions/postfix.rs and struct-lit helpers; AST for headed bodies that are not only named fields.
- Keep record field lists: Point.{ x: 1, y: 2 }.
- Accept element / entry lists for [T], [T#N], [K: V].
- Accept a single expression body for scalars and assertions.
- Accept empty {} for empty collections (and existing empty/unit cases).
- Nested list bodies may be bare .{ … } or plain [ … ]; both elaborate against the element type.
- Keep E0320 for retired dotless Type { }.
- Formatter prints headed forms; it does not rewrite them into typed bindings.

## 3. Sema
Owned: crates/jet-sema StructLit path (CheckerItems::check_struct_lit and/or a shared typed-literal elaborator), CheckerInfer/expr.rs StructLit arm.
- Resolve the head type (named, list, fixed array, map, scalar, generic apps).
- Set expected_type from the head; elaborate the body; never insert from_* conversions.
- Scalar literal bodies use comptime range checks in the E0135 family (D-RANGETYPE1).
- A mismatched non-literal body is the ordinary type error; teach from_* when the author wanted a conversion.
- Amend D-EMPTY: [T].{} is explicit empty; bare [] keeps contextual inference.

## 4. Lowering / TIR / codegen
- Lower headed literals to the same TIR shapes as today’s expected-type literals and struct construction.
- No new runtime. Codegen stays dumb (I3).
- Prove jet run and JIT parity on the new examples.

## 5. Examples (I5)
- Add examples/features/types/typed_literal_head.jet (or extend dot_construction.jet) covering: U8.{ 250 }, [U8].{ 42, 0, 0 }, [U8#3].{ 255, 128, 0 }, [String: Int].{}, Int.{ fetch_rows() }-style assertion, nested [[U8]].{ .{ 1, 0 }, [0, 1] }.
- Update examples that still put the type only on the binding when a head is the right spelling.
- Bless examples/features/expected/**/*.out.

## 6. Diagnostics / UI snapshots (I4)
- Prefer ordinary mismatch diagnostics; add a new code only if a body shape needs its own what/why/fix.
- Range overflow stays in the E0135 family with UI snapshots.
- No snapshot means no new diagnostic (I4).

## 7. Acceptance tests
- Parser/golden coverage for each head kind.
- Sema: match OK; mismatch fails; no silent convert; [T].{} vs contextual [].
- scripts/agent/jet-env cargo test (scoped) + jet run on the new example; UI snapshot tests green.
- Meet and verify criteria 1–4 plus the added implementation criteria below.

Land this card before #781 and #782. Those cards rewrite bindings onto these heads.

questions.text: We must ensure full expert control & auditability. We want magic out of the box for beginners but experts need to be able to see the inner workings & control as needed. Reconsider this ballot with devils advocate, make it best in the world, ensure ergonomics, magic, and full control are all considered. Tell my why your new option set is best, why you recommend your new recommendation, and how it compares to other languages
questions.answer: Updated D-WASM1. New rec: C, not pure inference. Default is inferred from effects and browser API use, but experts can pin `#Wasm`, `#Js`, and `#WasmExport`, then inspect `jet build --target web --explain-partition`. Devil’s advocate: overrides can create unsound crossings. Patch: sema checks all boundary types/effects, rejects browser handles in WASM, emits a bridge manifest, and snapshots boundary diagnostics. Compared to Next/SvelteKit: similar magic boundary inference, stronger typed bridge/audit story. Compared to Rust wasm-bindgen: less manual glue, more front-end-owned diagnostics.

questions.text: Why A not B? Is there a reason not to use B? it seems like it may be helpful to sometimes have the module level declaration
questions.answer: Reason for A over pure B: required module declarations make every beginner learn partitioning before rendering a page. But the module-level control is useful, so I folded it into A: default partitioning comes from `Browser` effect inference, and experts can add `#Target(Wasm)` / `#Target(Js)` at module level with sema validation. D-WASM1 now reflects that hybrid.

cards.body:
Ratified decision: D-WD11 = B (Typed target profiles (recommended)).
Source ballot: docs/ballots/world-domination-review-2026-07-06.md.

How Jet scales down to microcontrollers, kernels, and no-OS targets.

Chosen direction: Board/target profiles make hidden defaults explicit only when embedded/kernels are selected. Expert controls memory, linker, allocator, panic, volatile, and audit output. Weakness fixed: normal Jet never sees target jargon.

Guardrails:
- Preserve magic defaults plus full expert control from the ballot.
- Before adding any new user-typeable syntax, manifest field, command spelling, marker, provider prefix, or diagnostic code, raise a follow-up Tower ballot.
- No implementation card may ship a stub: docs, examples, diagnostics, tests, and verification must land with behavior.

Carry target, memory, linker, allocator, panic, volatile, ABI, startup, and audit facts through manifest/package model, sema, TIR, codegen, and build. Preserve I1/#Unsafe gates and transitive memory facts. Prove real Linux freestanding/QEMU plus representative MCU artifacts, linker scripts/maps, no-host-runtime rejection, deterministic cross-builds, size/budget reports, and AOT-only honesty where dev/JIT cannot run.

Best-in-class bar: Go encoding/* breadth with serde-quality fidelity (existing JSON/TOML/YAML/CSV adapters are already full-fidelity — keep that bar).

Gaps: XML parse/serialize (full, namespace-aware); one canonical binary interchange format (MessagePack or CBOR — pick one, I8; owner ballot); JSON Lines streaming read/write; streaming/incremental (pull) parsing for large JSON/CSV inputs with bounded memory; canonical/stable-key-order JSON output for hashing and diffing; base32; URL-safe base64 variant (verify what encoding.base64 already covers). All through the same Data tree + @[Codable] derive so decode<T> works uniformly.

Done means: each new format is a full adapter (not a lossy subset) with examples + golden tests, or a recorded non-goal. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).

cards.title: corelib audit: core.http — client/server parity with Go net/http + requests ergonomics
cards.body:
Best-in-class bar: Go net/http server completeness with Python requests/httpx client ergonomics. Client HTTPS-by-default (D-TLS1) and server TLS (D-TLSSERVE1) shipped — audit the rest.

Client gaps to audit: connection pooling/keep-alive; redirect policy control; cookie jar; multipart upload and form encoding; streaming request and response bodies (bounded memory); per-phase timeouts (connect/read/total); proxy support (env-standard); transparent gzip decompression; HTTP/2; typed URL input (consumes the core.url card).

Server gaps to audit: router with path params and wildcards; middleware chain; streaming responses and server-sent events; graceful shutdown; request size/time limits (safe defaults — I1); static file serving with range requests; access logging via core.log.

WebSocket client + server: likely its own module name (owner ballot). Done means: audit table plus shipped gaps with example servers/clients under golden tests; a realistic REST service example needs no third-party anything. Ballot gates: any new user-facing module name, function surface, or syntax is an owner decision (queue ballots before code); any external dep stays behind the FFI bridge pattern (I6).
cards.plan: Finish D-HTTPDEPTH1/A on typed core.url/core.mime/core.net: Client/Server/Router/middleware, pooling/keepalive, redirects, cookies, forms/multipart, bounded streaming, phase timeouts, proxy, compression, TLS, SSE, limits, static ranges, logging, and graceful shutdown. Apply HTTP-CORE2/CLIENT2/SERVER2 and D-DEP-HTTP2=B exactly. HTTP/2 is a transport upgrade; WebSocket lives only in core.ws per D-WS1=B. Prove hostile protocol framing, smuggling/limits/disconnects, real client/server/browser interop, AOT/dev parity, examples/docs, and no facade.

Audit complete; no source edits. core.data currently has only whole-text CSV and JSON ingest returning DecodeError and in-memory Table, Series, and LazyFrame operations. The canonical core.encoding CSV and JSON readers already provide bounded pull, synchronous backpressure, EncodingLimits, stable EOF, latched EncodingError, handle ownership, and partial-I/O location and cause. core.data has no typed stream adapter, data-specific retained-state limits, cancellation proof, or large-data allocation proof. Current analytics return 0.0 for empty reducers, clamp quantiles, coerce nonpositive rolling widths to one, leave NaN, infinity, signed zero, overflow, and precision without a normative law, concatenate pivot keys through a colliding delimiter, and can emit negative SVG widths. cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #296 criterion 9. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #296 govern this slice.
cards.plan: Review starts only after every producer closes. #710 first resolves its open XML projection ballot and finishes XML. #711 hostile-stream and #712 edition-surface work can proceed in parallel. #713 then proves whole/stream and execution-tier parity on those final engines. #714 pins all official and hostile corpora, examples, goldens, docs, and diagnostics against the shipped behavior. #715 reviews the clean integrated range after #710 through #714 close; it does not repair producer code or certify partial work. Preserve earlier accepted checkpoints as scoped history, not final proof. Reviewer procedure: 1. Record authority, base and tip, producer identities, reviewer identity/model/effort, target facts, and clean status. Read the full integrated diff and map every #710-#714 criterion to implementation and test evidence. 2. Verify every corpus manifest before use. Check URL/version, license/notice, SHA-256, case count, transformation provenance, and test reachability. Separate published oracle vectors from local hostile cases. 3. Run published expected-value and byte vectors for JSON/JCS, CSV, XML/Namespaces/C14N, CBOR, and base encodings. Run an independent implementation for interoperable cases, record its exact version and command, and classify each variance by standard clause and selected profile. Product code gains no oracle dependency. 4. Trace tests to the production whole/stream engines, host I/O, allocator, terminal state, migration, tier, and diagnostic paths. Reject delimiter scanners, transcript comparison, generated-source substitution, fallback masking, and test-only codecs. 5. Run negative controls for omitted or changed corpus rows, bad hashes, wrong outputs, every hostile I/O fault, terminal-repeat drift, allocator and limit crossings, XML external access, migration drift, and backend substitution. Each control must make the named oracle red, then be removed. 6. Run every split up to 4096 bytes, 32 saved deterministic chunk plans above it, endpoint and overflow limits, and three clean repetitions per supported platform and tier. Preserve seeds, oracle/tool versions, outputs, first differences, and timings. 7. Report only concrete findings. Producers fix them. Reviewer rechecks material fixes, reruns exact affected proofs, then verifies #715 and parent #296 criterion 9 with commit-bound evidence.

cards.title: JIT: reject gaps honestly without AOT fallback
cards.body: Inherited from umbrella #688 criterion 2. No new scope. Ratified decisions on #688 govern this slice.
cards.plan: Authority is D-VERDICT-687-1. Default jet run uses JIT. jet build and jet run --release use AOT. A JIT gap is a compiler defect, not a fallback. Current dispatch violates that law. Default jet run enters run_compile_cmd and builds native Rust. Default jet dev constructs CraneliftBackend over AotFallbackBackend over InterpreterBackend. Hot swap and restart use the same ladder. CraneliftBackend delegates on a missing program or any JIT compile error. AotFallbackBackend compiles and runs AOT, then uses the interpreter when AOT is unavailable. Interpreter.rs also reruns an E0953 JIT result through AOT. That retry can duplicate effects. Explicit jet dev --interpret correctly uses InterpreterBackend and E2201. No E2211 source, registry row, snapshot, explain entry, or CLI test exists. Use this exact diagnostic copy. What: Jet JIT has a compiler gap for this checked program. Why: jet run uses the JIT lens and does not hide a JIT compiler gap by running AOT. Fix: run jet build <file> and the binary for now, then report E2211 with the detail below. Detail: JIT gap in {function}: {reason}. Attach the entry function span when available. Keep raw Rust and rustc text hidden. Return exit 101 because the exit table defines compiler defects as ICE. A watching dev session prints E2211, keeps the last good state, and continues. One-shot dev and default run exit 101. --try-anyway applies only to interpreter E2201 and never bypasses E2211. Implement in one order. First change api_debug try_resident, hot_swap, and restart from Option to Result and preserve unsupported host, lowering, safety, compilation, and panic reasons. Then make CraneliftBackend strict and remove its fallback generic. Delete AotFallbackBackend and its native subprocess runner after all product callers move. Keep InterpreterBackend only for explicit --interpret. Remove the E0953 AOT retry. Route default run to the same strict Cranelift backend. Keep build and run --release on CmdCompile AOT. Update watch, restart, and swap so a failed edit retains the last good runtime. Register E2211 under the JIT diagnostics area. Add the exact what, why, and fix row. Update the stale dev-loop prose. Add a rendered tests/dev/jit_gap.txt snapshot and generated error reference. Test supported JIT run, each gap class, unsupported host, no duplicate effects, watch recovery, one-shot exit 101, JSON, color, NO_COLOR, explain, default run, build, release run, and explicit interpreter. Re-run the #727 strict corpus gate. Do not add a daemon, alternate runner, new cache, or runtime AOT fallback.

cards.title: Script-speed run loop: cached re-run, jet dev signpost, start budget
cards.body:
Persona audit 2026-07-23: every `jet run` costs 12-14s, even when the file did not change. `jet dev` runs the same file in 4.7s, but `jet run` never mentions it. Python starts at once. The focused agent audit also measured an unchanged process example at 36.38s through the required development environment. This gap decides the script persona and blocks Jet from replacing Bash, Python, and Node for short agent tasks.

Work:
- An unchanged file re-runs from cache with no recompile.
- `jet run` prints one tip line when a compile is slow: point at `jet dev`.
- Measure and enforce cold/warm script budgets against matched Bash, Python, and Node tasks.

Rides #687/#688 (jet run = JIT lens) and #439 (watch engine). The self-host era work (#666/#669) is the long game; this card owns the Epoch 3 daily-driver feel.

cards.title: Anonymous union types: decide before the stdlib bakes casts in
cards.body:
Promotes the union half of idea b4eclxq. The any half is ALREADY DECIDED: D-ANY-JAI1 (syntax-decisions.md:169-172) ratified trait-bounded heterogeneous varargs and rejected a general Any top type. That rejection is law and is not reopened here.

The open question: does Jet ever get anonymous union types (Int | String), or do named enums stay the only union? Why now (lessons-learned, Go generics): the encoding/data/web wave (#296/#307/#706-#709) is baking APIs that need the answer, and a missing type capability fossilizes casts into a stdlib.

Ballot D-UNIONTYPE1 on this card picks. Implementation follows ratification.
cards.plan: Implement ratified D-UNIONTYPE1=A as structural enum sugar, not a second sum mechanism. Add Type::Union with one canonicalizer that recursively flattens members, removes exact duplicates, and sorts by canonical source spelling; define parser precedence so T ? E1 | E2 places the union on the error side. Extend formatting, type traversal, equality/display, API snapshots, semantic index, and LSP to use that canonical form. In sema, allow only concrete closed member types, add implicit member-to-union widening at binding, argument, return, field, and error-propagation boundaries, and preserve exact union identity elsewhere. Extend union match heads to resolve an exact member type and feed the existing enum exhaustiveness and binding checks. Lower each canonical union to one deterministic compiler-generated enum emitted once per resolved union, with injection and match operations carried explicitly in TIR so codegen remains mechanical and native/web/dev agree. Extend Codable synthesis so each member encodes normally and decode selects a unique compatible wire shape; reject ambiguous or unsupported shapes in sema with registered UI diagnostics. Keep named-enum crossings explicit through ordinary match-based conversion functions and add no Any or cast escape. Update the syntax decision log and examples, regenerate grammar/tooling artifacts, bless snapshots, and run focused parser/formatter/sema/serde/golden plus AOT/dev/web parity checks.

cards.title: Browser debugging: source maps for the web target
cards.body:
Field audit TypeScript row: the browser is the runtime and feedback is live. Jet ships a web/canvas target, but devtools cannot step Jet lines.

Work: emit source maps for the JS/Wasm output so browser devtools show and step Jet source. The compiler already maps Jet lines to generated Rust for diagnostics (Source/Compiler.rs SourceMap) — extend that chain to the browser. Rides the web wave (#123, #701-#705).

Flip test: set a breakpoint on a Jet line in browser devtools and step.
cards.plan: 1. Reuse `TStmt::LineMarker` for web output. Do not add a second source-location model. 2. Add a std-only Source Map v3 encoder with stable source order. Use UTF-16 columns for JavaScript. 3. Record generated JavaScript positions before each emitted TIR statement. Emit `app.js.map` and its relative `sourceMappingURL`. 4. Compile Wasm with line data. Read rustc's Wasm line table after compilation. Join generated Rust lines to Jet lines through existing markers. 5. Emit Wasm byte-offset mappings in `app.wasm.map`. Put the relative map URL in the Wasm `sourceMappingURL` custom section. 6. Default, debug, and CI web builds include exact Jet bytes in `sourcesContent`. Release builds emit no maps or map references. 7. Use project-relative source names with `/` separators. Never emit absolute host paths. 8. Add both map files to build output, atomic dev swaps, static serving, and last-good rebuild behavior. 9. Reuse the current Chromium CDP harness. Prove Jet breakpoints and stepping in JavaScript and Wasm. 10. Run focused web tests and fresh review. If Wasm decoding needs a new tool or crate, stop and raise a dependency ballot.

cards.title: Toolchain telemetry and trust policy
cards.body:
Lessons-learned gap 2 (2026-07-23): Go's telemetry episode and Audacity show that even well-intentioned opt-out telemetry burns trust permanently. Nothing on the board mentions telemetry — deciding it implicitly by code later is the expensive path.

Ballot D-TELEMETRY1 on this card decides: opt-in only vs none at all, and exactly what jet/jetpack may send over the network (registry queries included).
cards.plan:
Implement ratified D-TELEMETRY1=A and D-REPORT-SEND1=A only. No new owner choices.

1. Inventory every jet/jetpack network path. Prove builds and ordinary commands never open telemetry, crash, or usage endpoints.
2. Keep registry/package traffic limited to what the user-requested operation needs (name, version constraint, protocol necessities).
3. Ship or harden `jet report` as a local inspectable bundle writer that prints the path. Do not ship `jet report --send` (D-REPORT-SEND1 amends the illustrative telemetry example).
4. Document the permanent zero-telemetry promise in owner-facing tooling docs.
5. Add regression tests that fail if a background usage/crash sender appears, and CLI tests for local report bundle creation without network send.

Proof: focused CLI/tooling tests + greps/audit of network call sites. No full suite required for this card alone.

cards.title: Bare bindings: retire the typed binding forms
cards.body: Binding grammar collapses to name :: value, name := value, name = value. The forms name: Type :: expr and name: Type := expr are removed as an immediate clean break — ordinary parse error, no teaching/retirement window. Types ride the value (Type.{ } heads, .new/.from_* calls); names carry types only in signatures and fields. Corpus migration: ~206 typed bindings rewrite mechanically.
cards.plan:
blockedBy: none

Authority: D-BIND-BARE1=A (ratified). Amends S1 / D-BIND4. Prerequisite feature: #780 universal Type.{ } heads (D-DOTCTOR3 shipped).

Goal: A binding is always bare. Keep only name :: value, name := value, and reassignment name = value. Delete name: Type :: expr and name: Type := expr. Immediate clean break — ordinary parse error, no teaching window.

## 1. Syntax authority
- Add the D-BIND-BARE1 entry in crates/jet-foundation/src/Syntax.rs.
- Append the syntax-decisions.md log: bindings never carry types; types ride values or live on signatures and fields.
- Run jet devtools grammars.
- Update Source/LSP/Completion.rs snippets that still teach typed bindings.

## 2. Parser
Owned: crates/jet-parser/src/Parser/Statements/bindings.rs (and formatter Statements.rs).
- Remove the typed :: and := binding productions.
- Keep name: Type on signatures, struct fields, and other non-binding positions.
- Old typed bindings become an ordinary parse error — no special retirement diagnostic.
- Formatter never emits typed binding forms.
- Editor grammars match the parser.

## 3. Sema
- Local bindings stop carrying a required annotation for emptiness, sized numbers, and similar cases; the value head from #780 supplies the type.
- Signatures and fields keep name: Type.
- Sweep binding helpers that assume Binding.ty is present for ordinary locals.

## 4. Corpus migration (~206)
- Mechanical rewrite: drop a redundant annotation when the value already self-types; otherwise lift the annotation’s type onto the value as a Type.{ } head or assertion.
- Touch examples/, tests/, and Jet sources under std as needed.
- Update docs/spec/spec.md binding bullets that still list typed forms.

## 5. Lowering / TIR
- No new runtime for bare bindings already supported.
- Confirm destructuring and other binding variants still parse after the grammar cut.

## 6. Diagnostics / UI snapshots (I4)
- Snapshot the ordinary parse error for retired typed forms.
- Re-bless any UI snapshots whose fix text still shows name: Type :: / :=.
- Hand uninit trigger changes to #782; do not leave a typed-binding-only uninit path.

## 7. Acceptance tests
- Corpus grep: zero live name: Type :: / name: Type := forms in .jet sources (comments that teach the retirement are fine).
- Example goldens and formatter round-trips green.
- scripts/agent/jet-env scoped tests + jet run on touched examples.

Implicit lossless widening covers floats as well as whole numbers. An F32 moves on its own into Float, exactly as a narrow whole number moves into a wider whole number; nothing ever narrows on its own. This amends D-FLOATW1, which today makes mixing F32 and Float a compile error with a convert fix-it. Owner words (2026-07-28): "Ok, again we want beginner magic out of the box and full expert control. So let's go with option f but for both int and floats". With D-INTLIT-WIDTH1=F this is the ruled surface: one widening law across the whole numeric menu.
